### 📚 Documentation Issue Description

> Related: #55 (owns the evolve pages in both languages), #118 (owns the English Idea Tree page and records product status).

## Summary

The Chinese tree has ten pages with no English counterpart, the English tree now has three pages with no Chinese counterpart, and readers cannot tell whether a missing language means "not translated yet", "internal", or "unsupported". I would like each gap classified and then closed, translated, or labeled.

## Current state

Verified against PR #122 head f1e18c5:

- `docs/en/` has 38 pages and `docs/zh/` has 45.
- Ten Chinese-only pages. Nine sit under `docs/zh/developer-docs/` and one under `docs/zh/core/`:

  ```text
  docs/zh/developer-docs/evolve-standalone.md
  docs/zh/developer-docs/plugins.md
  docs/zh/developer-docs/runner-inheritance.md
  docs/zh/developer-docs/session-trajectory.md
  docs/zh/developer-docs/skill-library-management.md
  docs/zh/developer-docs/skill-library-management-mvp.md
  docs/zh/developer-docs/skill-library-management-m1.md
  docs/zh/developer-docs/skill-library-management-m2.md
  docs/zh/developer-docs/skill-self-evolution.md
  docs/zh/core/idea-tree.md
  ```

- Three English-only pages, all under `docs/en/developer-docs/`: `context-assembly.md`, `context-assembly-examples.md` and `runtime-core.md`. The path move introduced this gap: they were language-neutral under `docs/architecture/`, so before the reorg both language trees could reach them and now the Chinese tree cannot. `docs/en/developer-docs/agent-backend.md:273` and `docs/zh/developer-docs/agent-backend.md:273` also still say `docs/architecture/context-assembly.md`, a path that no longer exists. Those are plain-text references, so the link check added by PR 122 does not catch them. Fixing this is content work for a later step, recorded here because it is a real gap in the shipped tree.
- The PR 122 body itself lists bilingual semantic drift as follow-up work, so this issue does not own the content alignment of shared pages.

## What to write

1. Classify the nine pages under `docs/zh/developer-docs/`. Two are owned elsewhere: `evolve-standalone.md` stays with #55, and the skill-library drafts are recorded here while their consolidation stays with the PR follow-up. The pages that need a disposition here are `plugins.md`, `runner-inheritance.md`, `session-trajectory.md`, `skill-self-evolution.md` and the four skill-library-management files. Each is either translated (public), labeled as an internal design note, or retired. The public status comes from the capability-entries issue (#118).
2. Classify `docs/zh/core/idea-tree.md`. The English counterpart or replacement is owned by #118, so this issue records only the page-level disposition and the status label.
3. Give the three English-only pages their own decision: restore them to a language-neutral location, add Chinese counterparts, or label them English-only. In every case, fix the two dead references at `docs/en/developer-docs/agent-backend.md:273` and `docs/zh/developer-docs/agent-backend.md:273` to point at the new location.
4. Add a status label to every page that has no counterpart in one language, so a reader can tell "not translated" from "internal".
5. Add the missing language counterpart for every page classified as public.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each of the eight pages owned by this issue has a recorded disposition (translated, labeled internal, or retired), with maintainer sign-off for the unconfirmed ones.
- [ ] `docs/zh/core/idea-tree.md` has a recorded disposition, and the English page or replacement is delivered by #118.
- [ ] The three English-only pages have a recorded decision, and `docs/en/developer-docs/agent-backend.md:273` and `docs/zh/developer-docs/agent-backend.md:273` no longer cite `docs/architecture/`.
- [ ] English counterparts exist for the pages classified as public, and Chinese counterparts exist where the decision is to translate.
- [ ] Every page without a counterpart in one language carries a status label.
- [ ] Pages delivered by #117 and #118 land in both languages.

## Open questions

- Public status of plugins, runner inheritance, session trajectory, skill-self-evolution and the skill-library design notes (same confirmation as #118).
- Can the superseded `skill-library-management-m1` / `m2` / `mvp` drafts be retired, or should they be kept as history?
- Should the three former `docs/architecture/` pages return to a language-neutral directory, or is an English-only page with a clear label acceptable?

## Out of scope

- Semantic drift between shared pages such as `mcp-tool-protocol.md`, `subagent-orchestration.md` and `deployment.md`. PR 122 lists that as a content-owner follow-up, so it is not an acceptance criterion here.
- How a page without a counterpart is displayed on any downstream site. The public site repository is deferred for now.
- Translating internal design notes before their public status is confirmed.
- The English Idea Tree page (owned by #118) and the evolve sidecar disposition (owned by #55).

## Summary

PR 122 already reorders the indexes into a sensible first-use sequence, but the how-to list now opens with connector configuration and the Getting started section does not say what each page assumes. Deployment moved to `getting-started/deployment.md` and the literature case moved to `domains/literature-research.md`, so the five remaining how-to pages are connector configuration, JiuwenSwarm, network proxy, an evolution search, and ScienceMemory setup. > Related: #26 (skills tutorial, later batch), #55 (per-capability pattern for evolve),
> #49 (Idea Tree settings are currently overwritten at runtime, which limits what can be
> documented honestly today). Note: the JiuwenSwarm backend-reuse series (#84) reworks
> some of these areas in parallel, notably #101 (Idea Tree service), #103 (Usage), #104
> (remote hosts and NPU), and #105 (Plugins).

## Summary

Several capabilities have no user-facing entry point in the documentation, and PR #122
made the gap structural: it moved the capability pages into `developer-docs` and left
`core` nearly empty. A reader who finishes a first task cannot discover what else the
product does. I want short, verifiable entries for a first batch, plus one structural ask:
every confirmed capability should have at least one entry point on the user-facing side.

## Current state

Documentation-tree evidence at PR #122 head f1e18c5:

- Idea Tree: the only page is `docs/zh/core/idea-tree.md` (34 lines, Chinese only). There
  is no `docs/en/core/idea-tree.md` and no how-to entry in either language.
  `docs/zh/README.md` lists the page under core, so Chinese readers have a route and
  English readers have none.
- Web providers: `docs/en/reference/web-tools.md` (69 lines) documents providers, but no
  how-to walks a reader from configuring a provider to a cited result.
- Skills and Specialists: the closest pages are
  `docs/en/developer-docs/skill-progressive-disclosure.md` and the long case in
  `docs/en/domains/literature-research.md`. There is no user-facing how-to for finding,
  enabling, trying, or scoping a skill, and specialists appear mainly in developer
  material.
- Usage: `docs/en/developer-docs/web-frontend.md:26` describes the usage dashboard with its
  filters and CSV/JSON export, but no user-facing page explains where the page is, what
  the numbers mean, or how to export.
- Structural evidence: PR #122's classification moved `science-memory.md`,
  `subagent-orchestration.md`, `skill-progressive-disclosure.md`, `science-connectors.md`,
  `review-provenance.md`, and `sandbox-execution.md` under `developer-docs`. `docs/en/core/`
  holds only `evolve.md` and `execution-workspaces.md` (the Chinese tree adds only
  `idea-tree.md`), yet the language index calls that section "Core capabilities". Six
  capabilities named in the PR's own body have no entry in `getting-started`, `core`,
  `domains`, `how-to`, or `reference`.

These are observations about the documentation tree, not claims of stable public support.
Confirmation is an open question below.

Implementation evidence, verified at `main @ e09d01b` (re-verify on the branch):

- Idea Tree settings and view components ship (`apps/web/src/App.tsx:229` imports
  `IdeaTreeSettingsEditor`, and the tree renders through `IdeaTreeView` /
  `IdeaTreeCanvas`).
- A Web search and fetch settings group ships (`apps/web/src/App.tsx:777, 5057`).
- `SkillManager` and `SpecialistManager` ship in settings (`apps/web/src/App.tsx:5078,
  5090`).
- `UsagePage` ships (`apps/web/src/App.tsx:4327`) with filters and CSV/JSON export.

## What to write

1. Structural ask: give every confirmed capability at least one entry point in the
   user-facing buckets. The cheapest form is a capability map page in `core`, with one
   paragraph per capability linking to the deeper page in `developer-docs`. PR #122's body
   already acknowledges there is no concise core overview for ScienceMemory, subagents,
   skills, scientific connectors, or review/provenance.
2. Idea Tree: a user-facing entry plus an English page at `docs/en/core/idea-tree.md`,
   written from the Chinese source at `docs/zh/core/idea-tree.md`. This issue owns the
   English page.
3. Web providers: a how-to from configuring a provider to reading a cited search result.
4. Skills and Specialists: a how-to covering how to find, enable, try, and scope a skill,
   and when configuring a Specialist is worth it.
5. Usage: a how-to covering where the page is, what the columns mean, and how to export.

For the remaining candidates with unconfirmed status (Plugins, session trajectory, runner
inheritance, the skill-library design notes): record the product status (public /
experimental / internal) somewhere a maintainer can cite, and keep anything unconfirmed
out of the user path. Page-level disposition of the Chinese-only pages belongs to the
bilingual-gaps issue.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each first-batch capability has a user-facing entry in both languages with one
  minimal verifiable operation.
- [ ] The English Idea Tree page exists at `docs/en/core/idea-tree.md` and covers its use,
  status, and limits, using `docs/zh/core/idea-tree.md` as its source.
- [ ] Every confirmed capability named in this issue has at least one entry point in
  `getting-started`, `core`, `domains`, `how-to`, or `reference`.
- [ ] Each remaining candidate has a recorded product status a maintainer can cite.
- [ ] Entries link the existing reference and developer-docs pages instead of duplicating
  them.
- [ ] The language indexes list the new entries.
- [ ] No entry promises stability or scope that maintainers have not confirmed.

## Open questions

- Confirm the public status and supported scope of the first batch, especially Idea Tree
  and the cost semantics shown in Usage.
- Which of Plugins, session trajectory, and runner inheritance are user-facing rather than
  internal?
- Should the capability layer be one map page in `core`, or one short page per capability
  in `how-to`? Maintainers' call.
- How should this batch sequence against the JiuwenSwarm reworks (#101 Idea Tree, #103
  Usage, #105 Plugins), which change the very surfaces being documented?

## Out of scope

# [Docs]: Deliver the first tutorial batch: analyze a dataset, run a literature search

> First batch of the tutorial series proposed in #26. Related: #22.

## Summary

#26 proposes a tutorial series and runnable quick-start cases. PR #122 removed the
tutorial directory in both languages, so the first batch needs a new landing place and a
new numbering rule. I propose extending `getting-started/` as the learning path and
dropping numeric file prefixes, then making the quick start's first task concrete, adding
a short model-setup page, and adding two tutorials that end in a verifiable result. The
later #26 batches (skills, MCP connector, and result-tracing tutorials) stay in #26.

## Current state

- Neither language has a tutorial directory at PR #122 head f1e18c5. The learning-style
  evolve walkthrough is now `docs/en/domains/evolve-a-solution.md` (119 lines) and
  `docs/zh/domains/evolve-a-solution.md` (85 lines). The only long end-to-end case is
  `docs/en/domains/literature-research.md` (212 lines, ZH 210).
- Quick start is `docs/en/getting-started/quick-start.md` (62 lines) and
  `docs/zh/getting-started/quick-start.md` (64 lines). Section 4, "Run a first scientific
  task" (lines 46-54), now has five steps that name a CSV or PDF, the permission card, the
  message timeline, and the Artifact area. It still gives no single named input, no exact
  prompt worth copying, and no description of what a correct result looks like.
- Model setup is quick start section 3 (lines 42-44). There is no page that walks through
  the settings UI (model registry, global defaults, connection test) or the failure path.
- Quick start's Next steps (lines 56-62) links deployment, configuration, runtime
  behavior, built-in tools, and `developer-docs/architecture.md`. It links no first-task
  tutorial. The language indexes list getting-started with two entries
  (`docs/en/README.md` lines 9-10, `docs/zh/README.md` lines 9-10).

## What to write

First batch, in both languages.

1. Rework quick start section 4 into one concrete task: a named small input, the exact
   prompt, and the expected visible result.
2. Landing proposal. Put the new tutorials in `getting-started/` and drop the numeric
   prefixes. PR #122 assigns `getting-started` the job of install, deployment, and first
   successful task, and it added no empty buckets, so extend it rather than revive
   `tutorial/`. Proposed files:
   - `docs/en/getting-started/analyze-a-dataset.md` and
     `docs/zh/getting-started/analyze-a-dataset.md` (new)
   - `docs/en/getting-started/literature-search-and-report.md` and
     `docs/zh/getting-started/literature-search-and-report.md` (new)
   - `docs/en/getting-started/model-setup.md` and
     `docs/zh/getting-started/model-setup.md` (new)
   The existing evolve walkthrough stays at `domains/evolve-a-solution.md` and becomes the
   advanced follow-on. If maintainers prefer a separate `tutorials/` bucket, keep the same
   descriptive slugs there. I am stating this as a proposal, not a decision.
3. Each tutorial states its prerequisites (a working model configuration), its expected
   result, and links deeper reference pages instead of copying them.
4. The model-setup page walks through model registry, global defaults, the connection
   test, and what to do when the connection fails.
5. Update `docs/en/README.md` and `docs/zh/README.md` to list the new tutorials, and point
   quick start's Next steps at `docs/en/domains/evolve-a-solution.md` plus the two new
   tutorials.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Quick start section 4 names a concrete input, an exact prompt, and the expected
  visible result (EN + ZH).
- [ ] `getting-started/analyze-a-dataset.md` and
  `getting-started/literature-search-and-report.md` exist in both languages, each
  completable with a working model configuration and ending with something the reader can
  point at.
- [ ] `getting-started/model-setup.md` takes a reader from a fresh install to a tested
  model connection, or quick start section 3 is expanded to do the same.

  them.

The file names above are proposals. If maintainers choose a `tutorials/` bucket instead,
the same criteria apply with that prefix.

> Complements the still-open #46 (its release-link, verification, ordering, and naming
> asks are tracked there). Related: #1, #27, #29, #35, #38.

## Summary

The documentation now sends a new Linux reader to a single deployment guide, but nothing
helps that reader choose among the three modes, prepare the right host, or recover when
the first run fails. The README installation section is one paragraph that delegates to
the guide. I would like that decision path written down, in both languages.

## Current state

- `README.md` (57 lines) and `README_zh.md` route installation to
  `docs/en/getting-started/deployment.md` and `docs/zh/getting-started/deployment.md`.
  The installation section (README lines 38-40) names neither a release asset nor a mode,
  and the Requirements table (lines 30-34) is the only place that ties modes to operating
  systems.
- The guide is 427 lines in English and 451 in Chinese at PR #122 head f1e18c5. It opens
  with a three-mode comparison (EN lines 5-15). The table columns are Mode, What the user
  receives, Host dependencies, and Intended use (line 7). No column states supported
  operating systems.
- Operating-system support is scattered. The binary artifact names appear at lines 24-25,
  local mode says it supports Linux x86_64/aarch64 and macOS x64/arm64 at line 131, and
  the Docker prerequisites say Linux x86_64 or aarch64 at line 173.
- The binary section opens with "Build and run" (line 19) and teaches building the
  artifact from source. Nothing in the guide walks a reader from a published release asset
  to `serve`.
- The local service token versus a model API key is explained in the README (line 51) and
  the quick start (`docs/en/getting-started/quick-start.md`, line 30). Token rejection
  recovery appears in the quick start and in the Docker FAQ (deployment guide line 390),
  but the README links neither passage. #35 shows the confusion is real.
- The guide's only FAQ-style troubleshooting sits inside the Docker section (lines
  378-408: build failures, data-directory permissions, port conflicts, token rejection,
  degraded health, sandbox failures). Binary mode documents Bubblewrap (lines 64-77) and
  local mode carries a Seatbelt note (lines 134 and 161), but neither mode has an FAQ
  covering token rejection, degraded health, or port conflicts. The quick start explains a
  `degraded` status at line 38 without linking a recovery passage.
- #1 asked how to obtain the binary. #46 asked for release links, SHA-256 verification
  instructions, a deployment guide led by downloading rather than building, and aligned
  configuration entry names. The decision and recovery layers above are still open.

## What to write

1. A short "choose your installation path" block in the README installation section,
   before it delegates to the guide: one line each for the prepackaged binary, source
   mode, and Docker, saying who each is for, with links into the matching deployment-guide
   section. Mirrored in `README_zh.md`.
2. Add an explicit operating-system column to the mode comparison in both guides (binary:
   Linux x86_64/aarch64, source: Linux and macOS, Docker: Linux), and lead the guide's
   binary section with downloading a published asset before the build-from-source
   procedure. This is the remaining ordering ask of #46.
3. A first-run troubleshooting block for binary and local modes (Docker already has one),
   covering at least: token rejected and where the Connection settings live, a `degraded`
   health status and what it means for the Runner, a missing `bwrap`, and where the logs
   are. Linked from the README.
4. Wherever a download command appears, link the Releases page rather than a pinned
   version URL, so the text survives the next release.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] README (EN + ZH) states who should pick binary, source, or Docker before it sends
  readers to the guide.
- [ ] The mode comparison in both deployment guides states the supported operating systems
  per mode.
- [ ] The binary and local modes have a first-run troubleshooting block in both languages,
  linked from the README or quick start.
- [ ] Any download command links the Releases page rather than a pinned version URL.
- [ ] The English and Chinese paths describe the same confirmed behavior and platform
  matrix.

## Open questions

- Is Docker positioned as an equal path for new users, or as an advanced option? This
  decides how prominent it is in the decision block.
- The packaging output includes `SHA256SUMS`. Confirm whether the published release assets
  carry it, and if so, add the verification step #46 asked for.
- Do update and uninstall instructions belong in the deployment guide now, or in a later
  pass?
- Should this issue absorb #46's remaining verification and ordering asks, or leave them
  with #46? Maintainers' call.

## Out of scope

- Changing the release process or adding build artifacts.
- Documenting unsupported platforms.
- The product fixes tracked in #29, #35, and #38. This issue only links their recovery
  documentation.
- Reordering the documentation indexes (tracked separately).

items.body:
## Background

ScienceDiscovery is strengthening its end-to-end test coverage. We want to collect the complete user journeys that the community believes must remain continuously protected.

This RFC does not prescribe an implementation. It focuses on four questions: **What task is the user trying to complete? What outcomes must be observable? Does the scenario require a real model? Should it run as a pull-request gate or as a scheduled test?**

## How to contribute

Copy the comment template below and add one row for each proposed test scenario. Maintainers will periodically consolidate actionable feedback into the main table.

Guidelines:

- **Test scenario**: describe a complete flow from the user's goal, rather than an internal function or an isolated component.
- **Observations**: list user-visible outcomes and critical states, such as the final answer, tool calls, permissions, artifacts, citations, and recovery after a refresh.
- **Test method**: use `Mock LLM`, `Real LLM`, or `Both`, and explain why a real model is necessary when applicable.
- **Estimated token usage**: use `0 (scripted)` for Mock LLM cases; for Real LLM cases, estimate total input and output tokens for one run.
- **Estimated duration**: give the target duration for one case, excluding first-time dependency installation.
- **Priority**: use `P0` for basic platform availability, `P1` for core scientific capabilities, and `P2` for enhancements or corner cases.
- **Notes**: record environment requirements, external services, credentials, cost, side effects, candidate benchmark sources, or stability risks.

## Initial candidates

The following entries are both examples of the requested format and an initial backlog. The community is welcome to refine their priority, observations, estimates, and execution method.

| Test scenario | Observations | Test method (Mock or Real LLM) | Related feature | Estimated token usage | Estimated duration | Priority | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Basic multi-turn conversation and refresh recovery | The run completes; the second turn uses conversation history; message order, terminal state, and refreshed content remain consistent | Mock LLM | Session, Agent Loop, History, SSE | 0 (scripted) | 2–3 min | P0 | No external network |
| Tool call, permission, and continued reasoning | Permission moves from pending to allowed; the tool executes once; its result returns to the model; the Agent continues and finishes | Mock LLM | Tool, Permission, Runner, Agent Loop | 0 (scripted) | 2–3 min | P0 | Use a safe local tool fixture |
| Plan creation, update, and completion | Plan and step states remain ordered and correct; updates do not block tools; the final state persists and recovers | Mock LLM | Plan, Context, Workspace UI | 0 (scripted) | 2–3 min | P0 | Use a deterministic tool-call sequence |
| Subagent delegation and result return | The child Agent lifecycle is complete; tool ownership is correct; the result returns to the lead Agent; reasoning continues; refresh restores the state | Mock LLM | Subagent, Team, Tool, Context | 0 (scripted) | 3–4 min | P0 | No external provider |
| Generate and deliver an artifact | The file exists; deliverables are distinct from temporary files; preview and download work; provenance is traceable; the final answer references the artifact | Mock LLM | Workspace, Artifact, Provenance, Tool | 0 (scripted) | 3–4 min | P0 | Use a local Python or Shell environment |
| Literature review | The Agent searches multiple sources, retrieves and extracts selected papers, produces traceable citations, handles source failures, and delivers a review artifact | Both | MCP, Literature Sources, Governed Download, PDF Extraction, Citation, Review | 0 mocked; 20k–60k real | 10–30 min | P1 | Real run requires network access and may depend on source availability |
| Evolve a solution | The Agent defines an objective and evaluation, runs iterative candidates, preserves checkpoints and logs, compares results, and delivers the best reproducible solution | Both | Evolve, Runner, Artifact, Provenance, Review | 0 mocked; 15k–50k real | 10–30 min | P1 | Candidate source: Terminal-Bench-Science |
| Data analysis | The Agent inspects an input dataset, selects and executes a valid analysis, validates intermediate results, and delivers reproducible code, figures, and conclusions | Both | Workspace, Python/R, Artifact, Provenance, Review | 0 mocked; 10k–40k real | 10–25 min | P1 | Candidate source: BiomniBench-DA |
| AI model workflow | The Agent prepares valid model inputs, invokes the model workload, exposes execution progress, preserves outputs and environment metadata, and explains the result | Both | Scientific Environment, Runner, NPU, Artifact, Provenance | 0 mocked; 10k–40k real | 15–60 min | P1 | Candidate tools/models: Protenix, ProteinMPNN, and similar workloads; hardware availability may constrain scheduling |
| Simulation tool workflow | The Agent prepares a valid simulation, invokes the selected simulator, reports progress and failures, and delivers reproducible configuration, logs, and results | Both | Scientific Environment, Runner, Tool, Artifact, Provenance | 0 mocked; 10k–40k real | 15–60 min | P1 | Real cases may require licensed software, large dependencies, or specialized hardware |
| Memory graph | Research outputs are written to the graph with correct identities and relations; retrieval returns relevant prior context; graph-backed citations remain traceable after refresh | Both | Memory Graph, Context, Provenance, Citation | 0 mocked; 8k–25k real | 5–20 min | P1 | Mocked case can use the local backend; scheduled case may use Neo4j |
| Agent team collaboration | The lead Agent decomposes work across multiple specialists; child scopes remain isolated; progress is observable; results return to the lead and are synthesized without loss or duplication | Both | Agent Team, Subagent, Context, Permission, Trajectory | 0 mocked; 15k–50k real | 10–30 min | P1 | Include concurrent child execution and one recoverable child failure |
| Idea Tree research | The Agent starts an Idea Tree run, expands and evaluates candidates, supports pause and resume, persists the tree, and delivers the selected result with its reasoning trail | Both | Idea Tree, Evolve, Workspace UI, Artifact, Provenance | 0 mocked; 15k–50k real | 10–30 min | P1 | Validate both tree state and the user-visible explorer |

## Comment template

Copy this table into a comment. Add more rows when proposing multiple scenarios.

| Test scenario | Observations | Test method (Mock or Real LLM) | Related feature | Estimated token usage | Estimated duration | Priority | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Describe the complete user journey | List user-visible outcomes and critical states | Mock LLM / Real LLM / Both | List related capabilities | Estimate | Estimate | P0 / P1 / P2 | Add environment, cost, dependency, or stability notes |

## Suggested areas

- Agent Loop, tools, permissions, planning, and Agent teams;
- MCP, skills, Web Search, and Web Fetch;
- literature retrieval, paper download, PDF extraction, and scientific databases;
- artifacts, provenance, evidence, claims, citations, and review;
- context compression, long-running task continuity, and error recovery;
- local and remote Runners, scientific environments, NPU workloads, and background tasks;
- settings, onboarding, observability, and critical usability journeys;
- scenarios that can reveal issues only with a Real LLM or a real external service.

## Expected outcome

Community feedback will form a prioritized E2E case backlog, divided into:

- fast Mocked E2E cases executed for every pull request;
- comprehensive Mocked and Real LLM E2E cases executed on a schedule;
- real scientific-task acceptance tests executed before a release.

This issue is for collecting and clarifying test requirements. Implementation can be split into follow-up issues and pull requests by scenario.

items.body:
### 🚀 Background Description ScienceDiscovery's backend is currently the TypeScript `services/api` (port 4310, `http/index.ts` at about 3,500 lines, `store.ts` at about 5,600 lines, depending on about 50k lines of `packages/*`, with the agent loop also running in Node). The frontend `apps/web` talks to it through about 260 HTTP endpoints plus SSE. [JiuwenSwarm](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/jiuwenswarm) already provides general agent capabilities: multi-agent team/Swarm, skills and skill self-evolution, permission approval, sessions and projects, MCP, scheduled tasks, and the jiuwenbox sandbox. This issue proposes: **keep the existing TypeScript frontend, reuse JiuwenSwarm as the main Agent backend as much as possible, and keep the science-specific modules (evolve, idea-tree, memory-graph, artifact/provenance, etc.) as standalone backends.** E2E cases serve as the acceptance spec for the migration. ### Goals and plan **Short term (Sep 30):** 10 E2E cases pass with no quality regression, and the corresponding 10 scenarios are usable; release a minor-version RC. **October:** Refine step by step, complete the migration, and make all E2E cases usable. **Long term:** Gradually switch to the componentized version of JiuwenSwarm (the `AgentRuntime` public API) and evolve in sync with JiuwenSwarm; gate on contract tests, switching the chat core first and the remaining domains afterward. The 10 E2E cases will be decided by Zhang Yi by Sep 21. **Baseline version:** Fixed on JiuwenSwarm 0.2.6. The interface and event analysis in this issue was read from the local `0.2.5.beta1` code and needs to be rechecked against 0.2.6. ### Overall migration philosophy 1. **Reuse JiuwenSwarm first and do not modify it by default; intrusive modification is allowed when necessary.** Use its chat, sessions, team/Swarm, permissions, skills, MCP, and scheduled tasks directly. Intrusive modifications are applied as patches on the fixed version (0.2.6) and merged back upstream later. 2. **Keep the frontend contract unchanged and translate in one place only.** The frontend speaks HTTP + SSE (32 event types); JiuwenSwarm speaks WebSocket (`req / res / event`, about 400 methods). A new **adapter** does the translation, with essentially no frontend changes; the goal is to eliminate endpoints that need a wrapper to adapt. 3. **Scientific value stays in standalone backends.** artifact, provenance, review, evolve, idea-tree, memory-graph, and runner each have their own process, data directory, and token; the frontend reaches them through the adapter's reverse proxy, and the agent calls them through MCP tools. 4. **Each piece of state has exactly one owner.** Sessions and projects belong to JiuwenSwarm, science metadata belongs to each standalone service, and the adapter only handles what nobody else owns (run event log, settings and secrets, permission audit, usage statistics). 5. **Tests are the spec, and the agent implements by "red-to-green".** First turn the existing E2E and contract tests into an acceptance baseline that can target any backend, then implement feature domains one by one; behavior without a covering case does not count as migrated. 6. **Switching can be done in batches.** For routes not yet migrated, the adapter can fall back to the old `services/api` and switch traffic domain by domain (this requires both sides to share session IDs, see Open decisions). ### Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR UI["Web UI (apps/web, TypeScript, essentially unchanged)"] subgraph ADP["Adapter (newly written, Python)"] direction TB A1["HTTP + SSE routes (about 260)"] A2["Bearer auth, users mapped to user_id"] A3["run registry and event log (seq, resume)"] A4["Event mapping (32 frontend event types)"] A5["Storage for settings, secrets, permission audit, usage statistics"] end subgraph JW["JiuwenSwarm (reused, not forked)"] direction TB GW["Gateway /ws"] AS["AgentServer"] CAP["Sessions and projects / Team and Swarm / Permission rails
Skill and evolution / MCP client / Cron / jiuwenbox"] GW --> AS --> CAP end subgraph SVC["Standalone backends (own process, data directory, token)"] direction TB S1["artifact / provenance / CAS
extracted from services/api"] S2["evolve
Python already exists, TS orchestration layer moved in"] S3["idea-tree
split out of evolve"] S4["memory-graph
already a standalone service"] S5["paper parsing"] S6["runner + compute
environments, execution, remote hosts, NPU"] S7["science MCP services
biomedicine / UniProt / llm-wiki"] end UI -->|"HTTP + SSE"| ADP ADP -->|"WebSocket req / res / event"| GW ADP -->|"reverse proxy"| SVC CAP -->|"MCP tools"| SVC ADP -.->|"Fallback for unmigrated routes (optional)"| LEGACY["old services/api"] ``` In the short term the adapter connects to the Gateway's WebSocket (broadest coverage); in the long term it switches to the `AgentRuntime` componentized interface.
The two ways to connect the adapter, and a few facts about JiuwenSwarm's connection layer **The two ways to connect the adapter:** | | A. Connect to the Gateway's WebSocket (recommended for the first version) | B. Embed `AgentRuntime` in-process | |---|---|---| | Coverage | All about 400 methods, including team/swarm, skills, mcp, config | Only covers single-agent sessions, chat, permissions, and model and mode catalogs; the Process CLI docs explicitly do not accept Team / Workflow / AutoHarness root modes | | Types | Handwritten, no schema | Python dataclasses, typed | | Stability | Protocol is ready-made, validated by the React frontend and the TUI | Public API was only just completed (`f29c060c`, `8773691e`), stability unknown | **A few facts about JiuwenSwarm's connection layer (which the adapter must fill in itself):** - Identity comes from connection parameters (`user_id`, `session_id`, `mode`, `agent_id`, `app_id`) or request headers, and no token validation was found, so the frontend's existing Bearer auth must be done by the adapter. - `seq` and `stream_id` on event frames are optional fields, and no mechanism was found for replaying by sequence number after a disconnect, so the frontend's `runs/:id/events?after=N` resume relies on the adapter storing its own event log. - The payloads of `chat.delta / final / reasoning` are flat `{session_id, content}`; `chat.tool_call / tool_update / tool_result / ask_user_question / subtask_update / subagent_activity / usage_*` and similar keep their full payloads.
### Migration approach per module | Scope | Migration approach | |---|---| | Chat, sessions, projects, permissions, models, MCP, skills | **Reuse JiuwenSwarm + adapter mapping** (59 approximate mappings, 21 direct mappings) | | Runs and event log, settings and secrets, permission audit, skill library versions, usage statistics | **Adapter-built** (JiuwenSwarm has none, 66 items) | | Science toolset (run_shell, execute Python, web, artifact, etc.) | **Provided again as MCP** to JiuwenSwarm's agent (a new major item) | | artifact / provenance / CAS, review | **Standalone service**: reuse the existing TS packages plus a thin HTTP layer, no rewrite | | evolve, idea-tree, memory-graph, paper | **Standalone service**: the evolve orchestration layer moves into Python, idea-tree is split out of evolve, memory-graph is almost as is, paper gets a wrapper layer | | runner, environments, remote hosts, NPU | **Keep runner + pass through**; remote host and NPU logic moves out with runner, in the second batch | | Scheduled tasks, science gateway MCP | **Reuse directly** JiuwenSwarm's `schedule.*` and MCP config | | Frontend | Essentially unchanged; hide unsupported entry points and clean up dead code |
Full module migration table (current state → target → approach) Legend: **Reuse** = use JiuwenSwarm directly; **Adapt** = the adapter does the mapping; **Build ourselves** = JiuwenSwarm does not have it; **Standalone** = standalone backend; **Keep as is** = essentially untouched. | Module | Current state | Target | Migration approach | |---|---|---|---| | Chat and agent loop | `native-agent`: 128-round loop, parallel tools, loop-guard, deferred `tool_search` | JiuwenSwarm's agent loop | **Reuse + adapt**: `chat.send / interrupt / user_answer`; the adapter adds a run registry, event log, and SSE resume, and synthesizes events such as `run.queued / started` that upstream does not have | | Context assembly and compaction | `packages/context` (about 3.5k lines) | JiuwenSwarm's context compaction | **Reuse**, our own assembly is not migrated | | Sessions and projects | JSON blob in `catalog_state` | JiuwenSwarm's session and project storage | **Adapt**: `session.*`, `project.*`; `SessionDetail` is assembled by the adapter; deletion cascades to clean up runner kernel and memory-graph | | Permissions and approval | `governance`, epoch, `permission_authorizations` | JiuwenSwarm's approval rails | **Adapt**: approval maps to `chat.ask_user_question` + `chat.user_answer`, `permissions.*`; **build ourselves** the epoch and audit table | | Models, providers | `model`, models.dev catalog, AES-GCM keys | JiuwenSwarm config | **Adapt**: `models.*`, `config.*`; quota, timeout, and proxy go in adapter storage | | MCP | Custom servers, OAuth, Inspector | JiuwenSwarm's MCP | **Reuse + adapt**: `mcp.*`; Inspector needs the adapter to bring its own MCP client, whether OAuth is covered needs a spike | | Skill and review drafts | `skill`, review drafts | JiuwenSwarm's skills and evolution | **Reuse + adapt**: `skills.*`, `evolution.*` | | Skill library versioning | commit / 409 conflict / dryRun / rollback / diff / proposals (14 endpoints) | adapter | **Build ourselves**: JiuwenSwarm only has `versions.list` | | Sub-agents, specialists, plans | `task` tool, `specialist` (8 built in), `update_plan` | JiuwenSwarm's team, agent_templates, todo | **Adapt**: built-in specialists become agent templates; `todo.updated` corresponds to `plan.updated`; the reviewer checkpoint has no counterpart, degraded | | Settings, secrets, proxy, quota | About 18 settings endpoints, several encrypted credential tables | adapter storage | **Build ourselves** | | Files, workspace, trajectory | `workspace` (about 5.2k lines) | `files.*`, `container_file_http`, `trajectory_http` | **Adapt**: upload conflict policy and workspace binding are built by the adapter | | Usage and quota page | `UsagePage` | Session usage mapping, cross-session statistics built ourselves | **Adapt + build ourselves** | | Scheduled tasks | `scheduler` (43 lines), `agent_timers` | JiuwenSwarm's `schedule.*` / `cron.*` | **Reuse**; semantics of agent-set timers to be confirmed | | Science toolset | `packages/tools` (about 2.7k lines): `run_shell`, execute Python, web search/fetch, `task`, `update_plan`, etc. | Provided as MCP to JiuwenSwarm's agent | **New major item**: today's tools are all written in the Node loop, so a new set must be provided; the tool list needs to be inventoried one by one | | artifact / provenance / CAS | `artifact-manager`, `provenance`, `cas`, `trajectory`, etc., about 12k lines of TS, with the logic inside `services/api` | Standalone service | **Standalone**: extract into a thin HTTP service reusing the existing TS packages, no rewrite; about 40 frontend endpoints; artifact ingestion is triggered by tool results or workspace file changes | | artifact review, claims, evidence | `reviewer-specialist` | artifact service + JiuwenSwarm sub-agent | **Standalone**, the review agent is carried by a sub-agent | | evolve | About 11k lines of Python + about 4.3k lines of TS orchestration layer (`services/api/src/evolution/`) | Standalone evolve service | **Standalone**: **recommended** to move the orchestration layer into Python with its own storage; the LLM callback proxy (`/internal/evolve-llm/…`) is provided by the adapter using JiuwenSwarm's model config; does not overlap with JiuwenSwarm's RSI / auto-harness (the former evolves candidate science programs, the latter evolves skills and harnesses). Alternative: first extract the TS orchestration layer into a small standalone process, at the cost of keeping two tech stacks long term | | idea-tree | TS package (about 1.6k lines) + Python router inside evolve + `python-client.ts` | Standalone idea-tree service | **Standalone**: split two routers out of evolve, own state directory; wrapped as MCP tools for the agent; research stream SSE passed through | | memory-graph | Already a FastAPI service (`:17674`, about 10k lines, 27 routes, no LLM, no sandbox) | Stay standalone | **Keep as is**: writes change to the adapter listening on the event stream and then calling `/observe/*` (event side channel, not intrusive to JiuwenSwarm); the Neo4j password moves out of the API's SQLite; on session/project deletion call `/cleanup/*` | | paper | `paper_worker.py` (204-line one-shot CLI) | Standalone paper service | **Standalone**: wrap it in HTTP or MCP | | science gateway MCP | Three stdio MCP services (biomedicine, UniProt, llm-wiki) | Mounted into JiuwenSwarm | **Reuse**: write directly into JiuwenSwarm's MCP config, zero changes | | runner, environments, sandbox | `services/runner` (TS, `:4311`, 39 route groups, execution endpoints have HMAC signatures); micromamba; bwrap / Seatbelt | Keep as is | **Keep as is + pass through**; add an executor MCP so the agent can run science code; whether the sandbox stays with runner's own or switches to jiuwenbox needs evaluation | | Remote hosts, NPU (trial) | Logic is in the API's `index.ts` lines 1219–1450 and `remoteCompute`, not in runner | compute module | Moves out together with runner, about 20 endpoints, **recommended for the second batch** | | Plugins (plugin-sdk) | `plugin-sdk`, `plugins/http.ts` | JiuwenSwarm's plugins / extensions | **Adapt**, different mechanism, can be deferred | | Auth and i18n | `auth.ts`, `i18n/messages.ts` | adapter | Auth **built ourselves** (backend route for the frontend login handshake to be confirmed); i18n untouched | | Launcher, Docker, binary release | `services/launcher`, `scripts/binary-release` | Added to the Python backend | **New item**: packaging and startup | | Frontend | `apps/web` | Essentially unchanged | Hide unsupported entry points, clean up dead code (such as legacy `remote-jobs`), minor type adjustments |
### Interface migration overview The interface list has 259 rows in total (isomorphic aliases merged, not an exact route count), of which 20 are not actually called by the frontend. **48% need the adapter to write or adapt them.** | Landing approach | Count | |---|---| | Direct mapping to one JiuwenSwarm method | 21 | | Approximate mapping (combine or convert) | 59 | | Adapter-implemented | 66 | | Standalone backend | 64 | | runner / compute pass-through | 44 | | No migration needed | 5 |
Full interface list and migration approach (259 rows, collapsed by 13 feature domains) From `services/api/src/http/index.ts` and the three route files under `http/`, 259 rows in total (isomorphic aliases merged, not an exact route count). "Not called by frontend" comes from a grep over `apps/web/src`. The JiuwenSwarm method names under "Lands in" come from the `ReqMethod` enum and are candidate mappings; those marked "to be confirmed" have no clearly corresponding method found; the specific conversions for approximate mappings must be verified with real payloads in a spike. **Five migration patterns:** | Handling | Approach | Completion criterion | |---|---|---| | Direct mapping | The adapter converts the request into one JiuwenSwarm WebSocket request, waits for `res` (or converts to `event` for streaming), and returns it with fields renamed | L1 diff cases pass | | Approximate mapping | Combine multiple JiuwenSwarm calls or convert structures; cache or accumulate events in the adapter when necessary | L1 diff cases pass, plus dedicated cases for the differences | | Adapter-implemented | JiuwenSwarm has none; implement with the adapter's own storage (SQLite, sensitive fields AES-GCM encrypted), with behavior aligned to the existing `services/api` | L1 diff cases pass, and data survives restarts | | Standalone backend / runner | The adapter reverse-proxies after auth, carrying an internal token; SSE and NDJSON streams pass through as is; return 502 when upstream is unavailable | L1 cases pass, plus a test of the error shape when upstream is down | | No migration needed | Legacy routes, routes that already return 410 or are shadowed; the frontend cleans up the dead code in sync | Just mark it in the list, no cases written | Every row must have a corresponding case in the L1 contract diff test, or be explicitly marked "no migration needed", as checked by a script. | Handling | Count | |---|---| | Direct mapping | 21 | | Approximate mapping | 59 | | Adapter-implemented | 66 | | Standalone backend | 64 | | runner / compute | 44 | | No migration needed | 5 | | **Total** | **259** (of which 20 are not called by the frontend) |

items.body:
### 背景与本 issue 的定位 #84 已经给出了迁移理念、整体架构、259 条接口清单、32 类事件映射与模块级工作量，并推荐「新写一个 adapter 接 JiuwenSwarm Gateway 的 WebSocket」。 本 issue **不重复**接口清单与事件映射，聚焦 #84 未展开的一个前置问题： > 我们复用的边界，应该划在 **agent-core（`openjiuwen`）** 还是 **JiuwenSwarm（`workswarm`）**？ 这个问题之所以是前置的，是因为一轮只读代码盘点得到一个结论：**我们想复用的能力，大部分实质在 agent-core，不在 JiuwenSwarm**；而我们未来想改的基础算法（上下文组装、多 agent 探索），**替换缝全部在 agent-core**。边界划错，会导致 agent-core 变成传递依赖，出现「想改算法却不能自己决定 agent-core 版本」的结构性矛盾。 本文据此给出后端分层设计、代码结构、迁移映射与侵入分析。前端 `apps/web` 保持不变，本文只讨论后端。 **分析基线（只读，未改动任何仓库）** | 仓库 | 分支 | commit | |---|---|---| | ScienceDiscovery（本仓） | `main` | `3cb3570091ab1559edf356a9a20f9df8bfff764b` | | [JiuwenSwarm](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/jiuwenswarm) | `develop` | `cdf1d0fd4aa6b93f95565383e6e61913981af844` | | [agent-core](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/agent-core) | `develop` | `6dfda012193d09dc3908524d5f8ae406811d909f`（JiuwenSwarm 当前 pin 的是 `d0bd83352f5ef4070baf44d37e788ba692a95b37`） | 行数统计口径为 Git 跟踪文件，未跟踪的虚拟环境与构建产物不计入。 --- ## 一、能力归属：agent-core 与 JiuwenSwarm 的分工 ### 1.1 体量 **agent-core（`openjiuwen 0.1.18`，647,577 行 Python）** | 模块 | 行数 | 主要内容 | |---|---:|---| | `core/` | 167,221 | `foundation` 25,991 · **`context_engine` 23,999** · **`memory` 18,149** · `runner` 13,622 · `retrieval` 13,176 · `session` 11,223（含 `vcs` 1,331、`checkpointer` 1,834）· `single_agent` 9,982（agent 循环、`AgentRail` ABC、`AbilityManager`） | | `harness/` | 148,673 | **`tools` 47,454**（含 **`browser_move` 25,026**、`worktree` 3,388、`filesystem` 2,636、`shell` 2,000、`web` 2,649）· **`rails` 28,250** · `personal_context` 24,351 · `prompts` 10,992 | | `rsi/` | 86,605 | `harness_rsi` 53,685 · `artifact_rsi` 32,206 | | `agent_teams/` | 81,969 | `tools` 15,400 · `agent` 11,493 · **`workflow` 8,454**（swarmflow 引擎）· `team_workspace` 4,139 | | `agent_evolving/` | 56,772 | `agent_rl` · `checkpointing` · `optimizer` · **`ttse`** · `trainer` · `updater` | | `symphony/` | 51,049 | **`retrieval` 21,140** · `orchestration` 8,369 · `discovery` 3,225 · `evaluation` 2,019 | | `extensions/` · `dev_tools/` · `harness_providers/` · `harness_protocol/` | 55,226 | a2a · observability semconv · SKILL.md 解析 | agent-core 的自我定位是 SDK：`pyproject.toml` 里 `description = "openJiuwen agent-core is a feature-rich AI agent SDK…"`，配 49 份 `docs/specs`、21 个 `examples/`、`[project.urls]` 的 Documentation 与 Changelog。 **JiuwenSwarm 分两类。** 用「模块内 import `openjiuwen` 的 `.py` 文件占比」作为归属的代理指标： *自有实质（低依赖率，agent-core 无对应物）* | 模块 | 行数 | 依赖率 | 提供什么 | |---|---:|---:|---| | `jiuwenbox/` | 36,396 | **1%** | 沙箱：bwrap · Landlock · seccomp · netns · cgroup · 推理隐私代理 | | `gateway/` | 57,681 | **6%** | 渠道适配、7 个 IM 平台、路由、cron 调度侧、斜杠命令 | | `resources/` | 41,847 | — | 35 个内置 Skill | | `common/` | 22,673 | 17% | E2A 协议 2,962 · 配置 · 148 个 `ReqMethod` · 自动更新 | | `extensions/` | 16,525 | **5%** | 应用扩展、Rail 插件、扩展包 | | `server/runtime/skill/` | 14,727 | **6%** | Skill 包管理、归档、热更 | | `server/runtime/session/` | 14,217 | 18% | 会话持久化、**项目 Git 与按轮次 diff** | | `agent_ws_server.py` | 12,076 | — | WS 服务端，处理 106 个 ReqMethod | | `marketplace/` | 4,690 | 15% | Skill Hub 客户端 | | `a2ui/` | 2,691 | **0%** | 生成式界面 | | `instance_manager/` | 2,539 | **0%** | 单机多实例 | | `channels/` | 15,979 + 216,621(前端) | — | Web / TUI / IDE / 浏览器扩展 / 桌面 / CLI / ACP | *agent-core 适配层（高依赖率）* | 模块 | 行数 | 依赖率 | agent-core 对应物 | |---|---:|---:|---| | `agents/swarm/` | 6,066 | **87%** | `harness/manifest` + `agent_teams/rails` | | `agents/harness/common/tools/` | 19,006 | **74%** | `harness/tools` 47,454 | | `server/runtime/agent_adapter/` | 36,050 | **65%** | `harness` + `agent_teams` | | `agents/harness/common/rails/` | 27,211 | **50%** | `harness/rails` 28,250 | | `agents/harness/team/` | 14,301 | 48% | `agent_teams` 81,969 | | `agents/harness/common/rsi/` | 11,862 | 46% | `rsi/` 86,605 | | `symphony/`（Swarm 侧） | 8,142 | 36% | `symphony/` 51,049 | | `agents/harness/common/auto_harness/` | 6,761 | 33% | `agent_evolving/` 56,772 | ### 1.2 七条容易记错的归属 | 能力 | 常见认知 | 实际 | |---|---|---| | 浏览器自动化 | JiuwenSwarm | **agent-core** `harness/tools/browser_move` **25,026 行**；Swarm 的 `channels/browser` 是浏览器扩展前端 | | Symphony 技能编排与检索 | JiuwenSwarm | **agent-core** `symphony/` **51,049 行**；Swarm 侧 8,142 行是服务化封装 | | RSI / Skill 自演进 | JiuwenSwarm | **agent-core** `rsi/` 86,605 + `agent_evolving/` 56,772 | | TTSE | JiuwenSwarm | **agent-core** `agent_evolving/ttse`；Swarm 侧是配置开关 | | 四套记忆体系 | JiuwenSwarm | **agent-core** `core/memory` 18,149 + `harness/personal_context` 24,351 | | 多 agent / swarmflow 引擎 | JiuwenSwarm | **agent-core** `agent_teams/` 81,969，引擎在 `workflow/engine` | | 上下文压缩 | JiuwenSwarm | **agent-core** `core/context_engine` 23,999（6 个压缩器 + 4 个卸载器） | ### 1.3 JiuwenSwarm 相对 agent-core 的净溢价，对本项目是否用得上 | 自有实质 | 行数 | 用得上？ | |---|---:|---| | `agent_adapter` + `agent_ws_server` | 48,126 | ◐ 仅在「整进程复用 AgentServer」时白拿 | | 内置 35 个 Skill | 41,847 | ◐ 部分（xlsx/pdf/doc 等通用 Skill） | | jiuwenbox 沙箱 | 36,396 | ✅ | | Skill 包管理 | 14,727 | ✅ | | 会话存储 + 项目 Git | 14,217 | ✅ | | cron 调度侧 | 3,558 | ✅ | | Skill Hub | 4,690 | ✅ | | A2UI | 2,691 | ✅ | | gateway 渠道适配 + IM | 54,123 | ❌ 本项目有自己的 HTTP/SSE 控制面 | | 多端（TUI/IDE/桌面/浏览器） | 232,600 | ❌ 前端固定用 `apps/web` | **用得上的约 156,000 行。** --- ## 二、结论一：复用边界划在 agent-core，JiuwenSwarm 按块复用 四条理由： 1. **能力在 agent-core。** 只依赖 agent-core 就能拿到 agent 循环、上下文引擎、记忆、检索、47,454 行工具库（含 25,026 行浏览器自动化）、rails 机制、agent_teams 与 swarmflow 引擎、symphony、rsi、agent_evolving，约 64.8 万行。 2. **替换缝在 agent-core。** 想改上下文组装或多 agent 探索，用到的是 `ContextEngine.register_processor`、`ContextEngine.register_window_mutator`、`agent_teams/workflow/engine/seam.py` 的 `use_provider()`、`register_{rail,tool,subagent}_provider`、`ModelContext(ABC)`、`AgentRail`——**没有一个在 JiuwenSwarm**（详见第五节）。 3. **穿过 JiuwenSwarm 会造成双层 pin。** JiuwenSwarm 的 `pyproject.toml` 把 agent-core pin 在一个 git rev 上（当前 `d0bd8335`），并有 `make update-openjiuwen` 滚动跟随 agent-core `develop`。若我们经 JiuwenSwarm 间接依赖 agent-core，就**不能自己决定 agent-core 版本**——而所有替换缝都在 agent-core，这是结构性矛盾。 4. **装配成本没有想象中高。** agent-core 的 `openjiuwen.harness` 导出公开工厂 **`create_deep_agent(...)`**（约 30 个关键字参数）与 `DeepAgentConfig`（50+ 字段，全部带文档）。JiuwenSwarm 的 `agent_adapter` 36,050 行里，`interface_code.py`（2,809，code 模式）、`team_helpers.py`（4,411）、`evolution_*`（1,347）、`browser_runtime_security`、`statusline_setup_agent` 等是 **JiuwenSwarm 的产品特性**，不是 agent-core 装配。按本项目自己的产品面（无 IM、无多端、无 code 模式、无 team 模板）重估，**自建装配层约 4,000–8,000 行**。 **与 #84 的差异**：#84 把 JiuwenSwarm 作为复用单位、adapter 接 Gateway WebSocket。本方案把 agent-core 作为硬依赖、JiuwenSwarm 按块可选。两者不是互斥的实现路径，而是**依赖方向的取舍**，建议在第 0 阶段 spike 里一并验证后再定。 --- ## 三、目标后端架构 ### 3.1 三层依赖与一条铁律 | 层 | 内容 | 依赖性质 | |---|---|---| | **L0 agent-core** | `openjiuwen`：agent 循环、ContextEngine、memory、retrieval、tools、rails、agent_teams、symphony、rsi、agent_evolving | **硬依赖，本项目直接 pin 版本** | | **L1 JiuwenSwarm 可选块** | Skill 包管理、Skill Hub、jiuwenbox、cron 调度、A2UI、内置 Skill | **可选依赖，每块一个 port，rev pin** | | **L2 本项目自有** | 科学 rails/tools/explore、科学域服务、科学侧车、runner、产品控制面、Web | 自有 | > **铁律：本项目业务代码不得直接 `import jiuwenswarm`。每块 JiuwenSwarm 能力先定义一个 `Protocol`（port），再在 `adapters/swarm/` 下写适配器实现。** 理由：JiuwenSwarm 是产品不是 SDK（包名 `workswarm`，版本 `0.2.5.beta1`，无公开 API 声明）。把 import 点收敛到一个目录，漂移的爆炸半径就是那个目录；每块可以独立决策、独立回滚；agent-core 保持独立可见。 ### 3.2 进程拓扑 ```mermaid flowchart TB UI["apps/web（React，不变）"] UI -->|"REST + SSE，37 类事件"| API subgraph API["sd-api（Node，:4310，保留）"] A1["http/ · store.ts · 静态托管"] A2["设置 / 模型 / 用量 / MCP 治理 / 权限 / 插件"] A3["agent-client（新增）：驱动 sd-agent"] A4["internal（新增）：科学域服务路由"] end subgraph AGENT["sd-agent（Python，新增）"] L0["L0：import openjiuwen
create_deep_agent · ContextEngine · AgentRail
agent_teams · swarmflow seam"] L2["L2：科学 rails / tools / explore"] L1["L1：ports ← adapters/swarm ⁄ adapters/native"] end API -->|"窄契约：环回 NDJSON + 内部 token"| AGENT subgraph SVC["科学域服务"] R["sd-runner :4311（micromamba · NPU · SSH · kernel）"] E["evolve / memory-graph / paper"] end API -->|"环回 HTTP + token"| SVC AGENT -->|"环回 HTTP + token"| SVC AGENT -.->|"可选，本机 HTTP"| BOX["jiuwenbox"] ``` 四条边界：前端与 `sd-api` 的 REST/SSE 契约**不变**；`sd-api` 与 `sd-agent` 之间用**本项目自定义的窄契约**（不实现 JiuwenSwarm 的 148 个 `ReqMethod`）；科学域服务沿用现有的环回 + 内部 token；JiuwenSwarm 的接触面只有 `adapters/swarm/`。 --- ## 四、代码结构与迁移映射 ### 4.1 新增 `services/agent/` ``` services/agent/ ├── pyproject.toml │ dependencies = [ "openjiuwen==" ] ← L0 硬依赖 │ optional-dependencies: │ swarm-skill / swarm-hub = [ "workswarm==" ] ← L1 按块可选 ├── scripts/check_layers.py ← 分层护栏 └── src/sciencediscovery_agent/ ├── runtime/ ═ L0：只 import openjiuwen ═ │ assembly.py（DeepAgentConfig → create_deep_agent） │ session.py · events.py（→ 37 类 SSE）· model.py · permissions.py ├── context/ ═ L0：上下文三语义 ═ │ processors.py（register_processor） │ window.py（register_window_mutator） │ projections.py（active_skills / plan_state / trust 标注） ├── science/ ═ L2：只依赖 ports/ ═ │ rails/（证据门禁 · 评审检查点 · 溯源记录） │ tools/（执行 · 证据 · 图谱 · 论文） │ explore/（Provider 实现：PUCT / idea-tree） ├── ports/ ═ L1 抽象：纯 Protocol，零依赖 ═ │ skill_store · skill_hub · sandbox · session_store · scheduler ├── adapters/ │ native/ ═ 兜底实现，不依赖 JiuwenSwarm ═ │ swarm/ ═ ★ 唯一允许 import jiuwenswarm ═ └── transport/ ═ 与 sd-api 的窄契约 ═ ``` `check_layers.py` 六条断言进 CI： 1. `runtime/` `context/` `science/` 不得出现 `import jiuwenswarm` 2. `ports/` 不得 import `openjiuwen` 与 `jiuwenswarm`（纯 Protocol） 3. `adapters/native/` 不得 import `jiuwenswarm` 4. `adapters/swarm/` 是唯一允许的目录 5. **每个 `adapters/swarm/.py` 必须有同名的 `adapters/native/.py` 兜底** 6. `science/` 不得 import `adapters/` 第 5 条是关键：没有兜底，「可选」就是假的。 ### 4.2 迁移映射 | 现有 | 行数 | 去向 | 替代者 | |---|---:|---|---| | `packages/runtime-core` | 626 | ❌ 删 | L0 `core/single_agent` + `core/runner` | | `packages/context` | 2,439 | ❌ 删，语义迁 `sd-agent/context/` | L0 `core/context_engine` 23,999 | | `packages/model` | 1,465 | ❌ 删 | L0 `core/foundation/llm` | | `packages/tools` + `workspace`（工具部分） | 约 3,400 | ❌ 删 | L0 `harness/tools` 47,454 | | `packages/specialist` + `orchestration` + `plan` | 3,190 | ❌ 删 | L0 `agent_teams` + `harness/rails` | | `packages/governance` | 227 | ◐ 策略留 Node，审批迁 `sd-agent` | L0 `harness/security` | | `packages/provenance` `idea-tree` `memory` `cas` `artifact-manager` `data-source` `trajectory` | 13,675 | ◐ 加 HTTP 外壳成为 `internal/` 域服务 | — | | `packages/schema` `mcp` `mcp-sources` `skill` `plugin-sdk` `executor` `sandbox-capability` | 约 13,000 | ✅ 保留 Node | — | | `services/api/native-agent` | 1,121 | ❌ 删 | — | | `services/api/{runs,agent-run,bootstrap}` | 5,112 | ◐ 改写为 `sd-agent` 客户端 | — | | `services/api` 其余 | 约 25,000 | ✅ 保留 | — | | `services/runner` | 8,798 | ✅ 保留（M2 可选把隔离原语换成 jiuwenbox） | — | | `services/{evolve,memory-graph,paper,gateway}` | 23,045 | ✅ 保留 | — | | `skills/` 17 个 | 3,641 | ✅ 保留，经 `ports/skill_store` 读取 | — | | `services/launcher` + `scripts/binary-release` | 3,203+ | ◐ payload 增 Python 运行时 | — | | **新增** `services/agent/` | 约 8,000–13,000 | ➕ | — | | **新增** `services/api/src/{agent-client,internal}` | 约 3,500–6,000 | ➕ | — | **后端非测试 TypeScript 82,367 行中，保留约 66,400 行（约 81%）。** --- ## 五、改基础算法的路径（这些缝全部在 agent-core） ### 5.1 上下文组装 `openjiuwen/core/context_engine/` 是完整插件架构：`ModelContext(ABC)`（抽象方法含 `get_context_window()`）、`ContextProcessor`（钩子 `on_add_messages` / `on_get_context_window`）、6 个内置压缩器 + 4 个卸载器。四个改造层级，均**零源码改动**： | 层级 | API | 能改什么 | |---|---|---| | L1 注入 | `AgentRail.before_model_call(ctx)` 改 `ModelCallInputs` | 加删消息、加 prompt section | | L2 换处理器 | `@ContextEngine.register_processor` | 压缩 / 召回 / 卸载算法本身 | | L3 换最终窗口 | `agent.context_engine.register_window_mutator(fn)`，`fn: (ModelContext, ContextWindow) -> Awaitable[ContextWindow]` | **最终送进推理的窗口** | | L4 换整个模型 | 实现 `ModelContext(ABC)` 子类 | 整个上下文语义 | L3 正好承接我们现有 `packages/context` 的「model-aware 原子窗口选择 + 最终校验」。**待验证**：`register_window_mutator` 的执行点是否确实在所有 processor 之后。 ### 5.2 多 agent 探索 `openjiuwen/agent_teams/workflow/engine/seam.py` 文件头原文： > "The provider seam: the indirection that lets the engine be swapped. … The engine installs its `EngineProvider` for the duration of a run; **a different implementation … can install its own provider instead, and workflow scripts never change**." API：`Provider(Protocol)` 覆盖 `agent()` / `parallel()` / `pipeline()` / `map_parallel()` / `agent_session()` / `human()` / `budget`，配 `use_provider(p) -> Token` / `reset_provider()`。因为存在 `contextvar` 里，**科学探索 run 与普通 run 可在同进程并存**。 于是把 `services/evolve` 的 PUCT 搜索或 `packages/idea-tree` 的想法树升级成多 agent 分支探索，做法是实现一个 `ScienceExploreProvider` 装上去，**workflow 脚本一行不改**。 另有按名覆盖：`register_subagent_provider(name, factory)` 的文档写明「a later registration for the same name overrides it」，内置探索子智能体名为 `core.explore_agent`。 ⚠️ 注意两张表语义相反：`harness/manifest/catalog.py` 的 `add_descriptor()`（元数据）**拒绝重名并抛 `ValueError`**；provider 注册表（工厂）**后注册覆盖**。要覆盖内置算法走 provider 注册表，不要重复同名的 `@harness_element` 声明。 --- ## 六、侵入分析 侵入要分三种： - **A 型（源码侵入）**：必须改 JiuwenSwarm 的文件 - **B 型（协商性侵入）**：不改今天的行为，但要求冻结或新增扩展点 - **C 型（反向侵入）**：不改 JiuwenSwarm 一行，但**它的运行期假设侵入我们**——改进程状态、强制数据目录布局、注入依赖树 前两种此前讨论过，**C 型是这轮新发现的，也是「按块复用」的真正门槛**。 ### 6.1 C 型：三个全局副作用源 **(1) `jiuwenswarm/common/config.py` 在导入期修改 `sys.path`**（第 48–57 行）： ```python _user_config = os.getenv("JIUWENSWARM_CONFIG_DIR") if _user_config: _CONFIG_MODULE_DIR = Path(_user_config) elif get_config_dir().exists(): _CONFIG_MODULE_DIR = get_config_dir() if str(_CONFIG_MODULE_DIR) not in sys.path: sys.path.insert(0, str(_CONFIG_MODULE_DIR)) # 插到最前 ``` 进程级、导入即生效、不可撤销。若该目录含同名 `.py` 会**静默 shadow** 我们的模块；且行为取决于环境变量与目录是否存在，同一份代码在不同机器上 `sys.path` 不同。`get_config` 被 185 个文件使用。 **(2) `common/utils.py`（2,954 行）假定 `~/.jiuwenswarm` 工作区布局**：解析顺序 `JIUWENSWARM_DATA_DIR` → `JIUWENSWARM_HOME` → `~/.jiuwenswarm`，并期望其下有 `config/config.yaml`、`agent/workspace/` 等结构。我们若 import 依赖它的块，就必须在自己的数据目录下再造一个最小 JiuwenSwarm 工作区。 **(3) 依赖树注入**：`workswarm` 的 `dependencies` 含 `chromadb`、`faiss-cpu`、`playwright`、`tree-sitter`、`sqlite-vec`、`pgvector`、`opentelemetry-*`，以及对本项目完全无用的 `python-telegram-bot` / `discord.py` / `slack-bolt` / `dingtalk-stream` / `wecom-aibot-sdk`。 ### 6.2 C 型按块实测 | 块 | 依赖 `common.config` | 依赖 `common.utils` | `sys.path` 副作用 | **C 型等级** | |---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:| | **Skill Hub**（`marketplace/hub_client` + 3 个兄弟文件） | **0** | **0** | **无** | **无** | | **Skill 文件/归档原语**（`skill_files` `archive_store`） | 0 | 0 | 无 | **无** | | **jiuwenbox** | 0 | 0 | 无（本机 HTTP 服务） | **无** | | cron store | 0 | 1（一个路径函数） | 无 | **低** | | **Skill 包管理**（`skill_manager.py` 8,841 行） | **4** | 1 | **有** | **高** | | 会话存储 / 项目 Git | 多 | 多 | 有 | **高**（且与我们的 `catalog.sqlite` 双主） | | 产品 rails / tools | 多 | 多 | 有 | **高** | 由此修订接入策略： - **Skill Hub**：四个文件干净到可以直接 import，也可以照抄（Apache-2.0）。零 C 型侵入。 - **jiuwenbox**：**它已经是独立组件**——自带 `pyproject.toml`（`name = "jiuwenbox"`），依赖只有 pydantic/pyyaml/httpx/fastapi/uvicorn/python-multipart/mcp，**不依赖 `workswarm`**，Python 代码对 `jiuwenswarm` 零引用；JiuwenSwarm 自己也是通过 HTTP 调它。我们可以 `pip install "jiuwenbox @ git+#subdirectory=jiuwenbox"`，零侵入。 - **cron**：只要一个路径函数。建议照抄 cron 表达式与 store 语义到 `adapters/native/`，不为一个函数引入 `common.utils`。 - **Skill 包管理**：8,841 行会带来全套 C 型侵入。三个选择：① 在 `sd-agent` 独立进程里接受它；② 只取 `skill_files` + `archive_store` 两个干净原语，打包逻辑自己写；③ 不接。 - **会话存储**：明确不接，避免与我们的 `catalog.sqlite` 形成双主；会话回溯用 L0 的 `core/session/vcs` 底座自己做产品化。 **新增设计约束**：`adapters/swarm/` 每个适配器要在文件头声明它拖进来的 C 型侵入，由 `check_layers.py` 校验声明与实际 import 一致；未声明的 import 直接失败。 ### 6.3 A 型：必须改 JiuwenSwarm 源码的场景，已缩到 2 条 本方案下**不再适用**的四条：新增 `ReqMethod`（我们不跑 AgentServer）、改 `agent_adapter`（我们自己装配）、换协作调度内核（走 agent-core 的 seam）、复用 JiuwenSwarm 前端组件（前端用我们自己的）。 仍然适用的： | # | 场景 | 触发条件 | 处置 | |---|---|---|---| | **A1** | jiuwenbox 增加 macOS 隔离后端 | 要保住 macOS 源码模式**同时**采用 jiuwenbox（jiuwenbox 目前 Linux-only；我们的 `seatbelt.ts` 在 47 个文件被引用） | 上游 PR；或不采用 jiuwenbox，继续用 `services/runner` | | **A2** | `skill_manager` 解耦工作区与全局 config | 要接 Skill 包管理，且不接受 6.1 的 C 型侵入 | 上游 PR（改为构造参数注入）；短期用 6.2 的选择② | 另有 A3（`common/config.py` 去掉导入期 `sys.path` 变更）只在「后端完全合并为单一 Python 进程」的形态下出现；本方案的 Node + sidecar 形态天然规避。 ### 6.4 B 型：建议向上游提出的扩展点 | # | 对象 | 诉求 | 不给的代价 | |---|---|---|---| | B1 | **agent-core** | 明确 `register_{rail,tool,subagent}_provider` 与 `ContextEngine.register_processor` 的**覆盖生效时机窗口** | 改基础算法只能依赖未文档化的时机 | | B2 | **agent-core** | 明确 `register_window_mutator` 在处理器链中的**执行点** | 窗口权威降级为尽力而为 | | B3 | JiuwenSwarm | 给出**可外部复用模块清单**并脱离 beta | `adapters/swarm/` 全部建立在内部模块上 | | B4 | JiuwenSwarm | **Skill Hub HTTP API 版本化**（现有 `hub_asset_port.py` 是 Python 端口稳定声明，HTTP 层无版本） | 被动跟随；最坏退回本地库 | | B5 | JiuwenSwarm | `skill_manager` 路径/config **改为注入式** | 见 A2 | | B6 | JiuwenSwarm | `common/config.py` 提供**无副作用导入模式** | 单进程形态下有静默 shadow 风险 | | B7 | JiuwenSwarm | jiuwenbox 发布到 PyPI | 便利性诉求，可用 git 子目录安装替代 | **B1、B2 最该优先推动**——「改基础算法」的能力完全取决于它们。 ### 6.5 反向：我们会不会侵入 JiuwenSwarm 不会，且是结构性的：单向依赖（`workswarm` 按 extra 引入、jiuwenbox 按本机服务引入），JiuwenSwarm 对我们零依赖；我们不跑它的进程、不实现它的协议、不改它的配置语义。若要贡献科学能力，走 Rail 插件 / Skill / MCP 的正向 PR，对它是加法。 --- ## 七、工作量 估算口径：同语言搬运约 800–1,500 行/人周；跨语言重写含测试约 250–400 行/人周；协议与语义对齐按耦合点计。不含产品需求变更与跨团队协同开销。**未做原型验证，第 0 阶段完成后需重新校准。** | 阶段 | 内容 | 乐观 | 可能 | 悲观 | |---|---|---:|---:|---:| | M0-a | 证伪 spike（四个判据，见第八节） | 2 | 3 | 5 | | M0-b | `sd-agent` 骨架 + `sd-api` 的 `agent-client` + 37 类事件映射 | 10 | 14 | 22 | | M0-c | 分层护栏、`ports/` 定稿、`adapters/native/` 兜底 | 3 | 4 | 6 | | M1-a | 工具面迁移 + 13,675 行域包加 HTTP 外壳 | 12 | 17 | 26 | | M1-b | 上下文三语义 + 证据门禁与评审检查点 | 6 | 9 | 15 | | M1-c | 科学探索 Provider（PUCT / idea-tree） | 8 | 12 | 20 | | M2-a~d | 按块接 JiuwenSwarm（Hub / Skill 包 / jiuwenbox / cron） | 15 | 22 | 36 | | M3-a | 分发：Python 运行时进单可执行文件 payload（双架构）、Docker | 8 | 11 | 17 | | M3-b | 测试与 CI：增 Python 层；E2E 大部保留（REST/SSE 与 Web 不变） | 6 | 9 | 14 | | **合计（M2 全接）** | | **70** | **101** | **161 人周** | | **不接任何 JiuwenSwarm 块** | | **55** | **79** | **125 人周** | **M2 各块彼此独立**，可以只接 Skill Hub 不接 jiuwenbox，或反过来。这是本方案与「整体二选一」的主要差别：**JiuwenSwarm 从一次性决策变成逐块定价**。 **不可逆点**：M1-a 完成后，工具实现不再留在 Node 侧。M0 全程可回滚。 --- ## 八、第 0 阶段的证伪判据 | # | 判据 | 决定什么 | |---|---|---| | ① | `create_deep_agent()` 跑通一次带工具调用 + 审批中断 + 流式的会话，并映射成现有 37 类 SSE | 自建装配的 4,000–8,000 行估算是否成立 | | ② | `register_window_mutator` 注入的受保护段，能否存活到最终 LLM 窗口（构造一个会被内置压缩器改写的长会话） | 上下文三语义能否等价迁移，还是要接受行为回退 | | ③ | 实现一个最小 `Provider` 并 `use_provider()`，验证 workflow 原语被整体替换后行为正确 | 科学探索能否成为多 agent 范式 | | ④ | `pip install workswarm` 后做依赖裁剪试验，量出可接受的最小依赖集 | M2 各块的分发成本 | 判据 ①③④ 直接决定路线，判据 ② 决定产品行为是否回退。**在第 0 阶段之前讨论总工期意义不大。** --- ## 九、待决定事项 1. **复用边界**：agent-core 直接依赖（本 issue）还是经 JiuwenSwarm Gateway（#84）。建议在 M0-a 一并验证后再定。 2. **是否采用 jiuwenbox**：采用则获得 Landlock、cgroup、推理隐私代理，但 **macOS 源码模式会失去沙箱**（jiuwenbox Linux-only）。需要产品明确。 3. **是否接 Skill 包管理**：涉及 6.2 的高 C 型侵入，三个选择需要拍板。 4. **控制面语言**：本方案保持 `services/api` 为 Node（保全约 81% 后端代码）。若未来要合并为单一 Python 后端，M0–M2 完成后可平滑过渡，但会额外触发 A3。 5. **差异化定位**：如果本项目的差异化主要在科学域能力（工具、连接器、证据溯源、科学环境、NPU），现有分层足够；如果在 agent 算法本身（上下文、探索、检索、演进），则应进一步收紧对 agent-core 的直接控制。这决定第 5 节各层级的使用频度。 --- ### 补充说明 - 本 issue 的全部结论来自上述基线 commit 的只读代码盘点，**未改动任何仓库**，未建分支、未提 PR。 - 归属用的「依赖率」是「模块内 import `openjiuwen` 的 `.py` 文件数 / 该模块 `.py` 文件总数」，是**代理指标**而非逻辑占比的精确度量；每条归属结论另有行数对照或具体文件路径佐证。 - C 型侵入的判定口径是「模块文件是否 import `jiuwenswarm.common.config` / `jiuwenswarm.common.utils`」，是传递依赖的一级近似；真正接入前应在 M0/M2 用一次真实 import 验证完整传递闭包。 - 与 #84 互为补充，不替代。

items.body:
> Cross-tracking: [GitCode #106](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/106) (Chinese counterpart of this issue).

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Environment and reproduction steps are included.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What I was trying to do:** On a laptop screen, open a session with an in-progress Plan and read the progress in the right-hand Tasks panel (e.g. “3/8 completed · 3 in progress” and the Active badge).

**What I saw:** The Plan card in the workspace sidebar is clipped. The **Active / 进行中 badge is cut off on the right**, and the plan body runs off the edge. Progress is not fully readable at laptop width.

*(Screenshot of the clipped Plan card is in [GitCode #106](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/106).)*

The screenshot shows “Plan · main / 3/8 completed · 3 in progress” with the status badge sliced, and the English summary overflowing on the right.

**Expected**

- At typical laptop widths, the Plan card (title, progress summary, status badge, body) stays fully inside the sidebar.
- When space is tight, wrap or use the available width; do not clip the badge or body.
- Plan semantics stay the same; this is display only.

Not GitCode [#93](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/93) (left chrome stacking at ~900px). This is **clipping inside** the right-hand Plan card.

**Reproduction**

1. On a laptop resolution (≈13–14″ fullscreen, or a window clearly narrower than an external monitor), open a Session with an in-progress Plan.
2. Expand Workspace → Tasks.
3. Check whether “Plan · main” clips the status badge and body on the right edge.

Code pointer (not the acceptance surface): `.workspace-plan-section` titles use nowrap + ellipsis; the badge is nowrap. On a narrow sidebar the heading and body overflow instead of using the available width.

### Environment

- OS: Linux
- Browser: Chrome
- UI language: Simplified Chinese
- Viewport: laptop screen, workspace sidebar open, Plan in progress

### Additional Information

The screenshot also shows the Tasks fold heading twice. If that shares the overflow cause, fix it here; if it is a separate duplicate fold, it can be another issue and must not block “progress is not fully visible.”

### Version

Current product UI (recent `openJiuwen/sciencediscovery` main behavior).

> Cross-tracking: [GitCode #26](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/26) (Chinese original of this issue). ### 🚀 Background Description Research agents often produce scripts, logs, configs, and prose (`.py`, `.r`, `.sh`, `.txt`, `.log`, `.yaml`, `.toml`, `.sql`, …). Users need to read those files in the artifact panel, not download them or jump to a new browser tab. The current viewer has two gaps: 1. **Plain-text artifacts have almost no in-app preview.** Catalog kinds only cover dataset / figure / html / json / latex / markdown / notebook / report / structure. Files such as `.py`, `.txt`, and `.log` fall into `other`. `ArtifactModal` loads only a few scientific kinds as text; `other` has no preview branch, so opening them is often a blank panel. In the workspace file sidebar, only `.md` uses the in-app Markdown reader; everything else is handed to `window.open` and the browser. 2. **Existing source / raw views are not a code-reading experience.** JSON, LaTeX source, Markdown source, CSV raw, and notebook code are plain `
`: no language highlighting, no line numbers, and long files are hard to scan or compare.

The viewer should:

- open plain-text files in-app;
- syntax-highlight common file types;
- show line numbers.

This is a viewing-experience request only. It does not change artifact registration, versioning, or provenance semantics.

### Design Ideas

Keep the existing specialized previews (Markdown render, tables, images, PDF/HTML iframe, molecular structure, notebook cells). Add one shared path for “read as source.”

Suggested behavior:

- Open recognizable UTF-8 text in-app — not a blank panel, and not a new browser tab by default.
- Pick a highlight language from the extension (and `mediaType` if needed). At least cover common research/engineering types:
  - plain text: `.txt`, `.log`, `.out`, `.err`
  - code: `.py`, `.r` / `.R`, `.jl`, `.js`, `.ts`, `.jsx`, `.tsx`, `.sh` / `.bash`, `.sql`, `.c` / `.h` / `.cpp`, `.java`, `.go`, `.rs`
  - config / data source: `.json`, `.yaml` / `.yml`, `.toml`, `.ini`, `.xml`, `.css`, `.html`
  - document source: `.md`, `.tex`
- Unmatched extensions that are still text: show as plain text, still with line numbers.
- Binaries, images, PDFs, Office files, etc. keep the current specialized viewer or download; do not force them through a text decoder.
- Markdown / table / notebook specialized previews stay; their “Source / Raw” views should reuse the same highlight + line-number component.
- Oversized files keep truncated preview (reuse the existing ~100_000 character cap) and tell the user they can download the full file.
- Highlighter library and whether to add `kind=text/code` are implementation choices, as long as the user gets highlighted text with line numbers. Do not change the artifact catalog or provenance semantics just to enable highlighting.

Out of scope:

- editing or saving files in the viewer;
- turning every file into a source view (images still show as images, CSVs still show as tables);
- a full IDE (folding, go-to-definition, diagnostics).

### Involved Public APIs

No new public HTTP API is expected. The viewer should keep using the existing artifact-version content and workspace-file read endpoints.

Possible internal adjustments (for implementation, not a product contract):

- load `other` / uncategorized text as text instead of skipping it as binary;
- if extension classification gains a `text`/`code` kind, use it only for preview routing and do not change the meaning of existing scientific kinds.

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- Artifact panel `ArtifactModal`: main catalog preview; `other` text must be readable.
- Workspace file tree: clicking `.py` / `.txt` etc. should open the same in-app text view, not only a new browser tab.
- Existing source views: JSON raw, Markdown/LaTeX source, CSV raw, notebook code, provenance scripts/logs — good candidates to reuse the same component.
- Artifact classification (`classifyScientificArtifact`): there is no text/code kind today; do not mis-label `.py` as dataset/report.
- i18n: new buttons / empty states / truncation copy must go through the existing message catalog.
- E2E: artifact panel, workspace file open, and existing Markdown/table/structure previews all need regression.

### Test Design and Test Plan

Functional:

- Open `.txt`: in-app full text (or truncation notice), line numbers; highlighting optional.
- Open `.py` / `.yaml` / `.json` and other common types: matching syntax highlighting, line numbers aligned with source lines (at least line 1 and the last visible line).
- Unknown extension, UTF-8 text: still opens as plain text with line numbers.
- Images, PDFs, structure files, other non-text: unchanged, not treated as source.
- Markdown artifacts: default remains rendered; Source view has highlighting and line numbers.
- Huge text: preview truncates, offers download, page stays responsive.
- Empty file: stable empty state, no error.

Regression:

- Markdown reports, CSV/JSON tables, images, HTML, notebooks, and molecular-structure previews still work.
- Workspace `.md` still uses the Markdown reader.
- Artifact download, version switching, and the provenance page still work.

Web E2E (required after changing the user-visible viewer):

- Open a text artifact in the panel; screenshot the highlighted, numbered end state.
- Open `.py` or `.txt` from the workspace tree; confirm in-app viewing rather than relying only on a new browser tab.
- Regression on one existing specialized preview (Markdown or CSV).

Formal E2E must not use the human trial port 4310 or its fixed data directory.

### Additional Information

Original request: support viewing plain-text artifacts, syntax highlighting for common file types, and line numbers.
items.title: [Feature]: Artifact viewer should preview plain text with syntax highlighting and line numbers

> Cross-tracking: [GitCode #105](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/105) (Chinese counterpart of this issue).

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Environment and reproduction steps are included.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What I was trying to do:** Drop a research file (e.g. `.pdb`) into the workspace of an empty session, then ask the Agent. The file already appears in the right-hand workspace tree.

**What I saw:** The main conversation column, still on the “What should we research?” empty state with **no run yet**, shows that upload as a **“Current workspace files”** card. The same file is already listed under Workspace files on the right. The conversation card is duplicate, and it reads as if it were this round’s artifact.

*(Screenshot of the uploaded PDB as a conversation card is in [GitCode #105](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/105).)*

In the screenshot, `6DZM_A_renumbered.pdb` sits above the composer as “Current workspace file · unpinned version”; the right panel already shows Artifacts 1 / Workspace files 1. No user message has been sent.

**Expected**

- Conversation cards show **only artifacts produced in the current round** (declared/generated this run).
- User-uploaded workspace files belong in the right-hand file tree (and on the user message if attached). They must **not** become conversation cards.
- With no current-round artifacts, the conversation column must not show a “Current workspace files” block.

This matches closed GitCode [#60](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/60) (show **generated** artifacts under the reply). It is not GitCode [#83](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/83) (list appears before the run finishes): here the **upload itself** becomes a conversation card, even with no run.

**Reproduction**

1. Open an empty Session (no user messages).
2. Drop a file into the right-hand workspace (screenshot used `.pdb`; other previewable uploads behave the same).
3. Observe the center column: a “Current workspace files” card appears under the empty state.

Code pointer (not the acceptance surface): `ConversationArtifactList` falls back to `currentFiles` and the “current workspace files” heading when `outputs` is empty; `App.tsx` feeds unregistered workspace files (including uploads with `previewKind`) into that list.

### Environment

- OS: Linux
- Browser: Chrome
- UI language: Simplified Chinese
- Scene: empty Session, workspace upload only, no message sent

### Additional Information

Keeping the upload in the right-hand file tree is correct. This issue only asks the conversation column not to repeat user uploads.

### Version

Current product UI (recent `openJiuwen/sciencediscovery` main behavior).
