## Summary

`docs/` holds a substantial bilingual documentation set, but it is only consumable as raw Markdown files browsed one at a time in the repository. I would like the docs to be **built into a static site and published on GitHub Pages**, with the build itself kept host-neutral so the same output can also be served from GitCode or an internal mirror.

## Current state

- 75 Markdown files: `docs/en` (31), `docs/zh` (40), `docs/architecture` (3), plus `docs/README.md` and `docs/images/`.
- Navigation is entirely hand-maintained index pages (`docs/README.md`, `docs/en/README.md`, `docs/en/explanation/README.md`, and the Chinese equivalents).
- No static-site generator config exists anywhere in the tree (no VitePress, MkDocs, or Docusaurus).
- GitHub Pages is not enabled on this mirror (`GET /repos/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pages` → 404), while `.github/workflows/ci.yml` shows GitHub Actions is already wired up here — so a docs deploy job fits the existing setup.

## Why this matters

1. **No search.** Answering "which environment variable selects the PyPI mirror" or "what does `needs-password` mean" currently requires cloning the repo and grepping. A reader who found the project from the README has no way to search the docs.
2. **No navigation.** Landing on a deep file such as `docs/en/reference/configuration.md` gives no sidebar, no page TOC, and no next/previous. The curated index pages have to be found first, and they are maintained by hand, so a new page is only reachable if someone remembers to link it.
3. **Relative links only work inside a checkout.** `docs/en/how-to/deployment.md` links to `../../../README.md#requirements`; that resolves in a clone and on a blob page, but there is no rendered docs URL to hand to a user, cite in an issue, or point at from a release note.
4. **Translation drift is invisible.** The two trees are not in sync — 9 explanation pages exist only in Chinese and have no English counterpart:
   `evolve-standalone`, `idea-tree-engine`, `plugins`, `runner-inheritance`, `skill-library-management` (plus `-mvp`, `-m1`, `-m2`), `skill-self-evolution`.
   A site with proper locale roots surfaces a missing translation instead of silently offering nothing.
5. **No versioning.** Someone running release 0.2.0 reads `main`'s documentation, which may describe flags, paths, or settings that do not exist in their build.
6. **It compounds the onboarding problems already reported.** See [#22](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/22) (make the product easy to understand, start, and use) and [#1](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/1) (how to obtain the binary package). A searchable, linkable docs site is the cheapest part of that fix.

## Proposal

1. **Add a docs site build.** [VitePress](https://vitepress.dev/) fits this repo with the least friction: it runs on the toolchain already required (Node.js 22.19+, pnpm 11.1.2), installs as another pnpm workspace package, consumes the existing Markdown essentially unchanged, and ships built-in i18n, local full-text search, and dark mode. MkDocs Material is a reasonable alternative if the maintainers prefer the Python side of the stack, since `uv` is already a prerequisite.
2. **Wire the existing trees to locale roots.** `docs/en` → `/en/`, `docs/zh` → `/zh/`, with a language switcher in the nav and `docs/README.md` as the landing redirect. Keep the sidebar in config so the curated index pages stay optional rather than load-bearing.
3. **Add `pnpm docs:dev` / `pnpm docs:build`** at the repository root, alongside the existing `build` / `check` / `test` scripts, so the site can be built and previewed locally without any GitHub-specific step.
4. **Add `.github/workflows/docs.yml`** that runs `pnpm docs:build` and deploys to Pages (`actions/deploy-pages`) on pushes to `main`. Because the canonical repository is on GitCode and this is a mirror, the workflow should be a thin wrapper over the same `docs:build` output, which can equally be uploaded to GitCode Pages or an internal server.
5. **Fail the build on dead links.** VitePress rejects unresolved Markdown links by default; turning that on catches the link rot that hand-maintained index pages accumulate, and makes the docs build a useful CI check in its own right.
6. **Optional, later:** publish a version per release tag so `0.2.0` users can read `0.2.0` docs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `pnpm docs:build` produces a static site from `docs/` on a clean checkout.
- [ ] The published site has working English and Chinese roots with a visible language switch.
- [ ] Full-text search covers both locales.
- [ ] Every page is reachable from the sidebar, and internal links resolve (build fails otherwise).
- [ ] Pushing to `main` republishes the site automatically.
- [ ] `README.md` / `README_zh.md` link to the published site.

## Open questions

- VitePress (Node, matches the existing workspace) or MkDocs Material (Python, matches `uv`)?
- Should the site root default to English, Chinese, or a language-choice landing page?
- Latest-only to start with, or versioned docs from the first release?
- Since GitHub is a mirror of the GitCode repository, should Pages be the canonical docs host, or a mirror of a site published elsewhere?

Happy to prepare the VitePress scaffold and the Pages workflow if the direction is acceptable.

## Summary

The tutorial section is a single page, and it stops right where a new user needs the most help. I would like the **tutorial series filled out** and a set of **short, runnable quick-start cases** with concrete inputs and described outcomes.

## Current state

- `docs/en/tutorial/` and `docs/zh/tutorial/` each contain exactly one file: `01-quick-start.md` (62 and 64 lines). The `01-` prefix promises a series; nothing follows it.
- Of those ~62 lines, sections 1–3 are environment prep, starting the stack, and pasting a model key — setup, not learning. The section that actually matters, "Run a first scientific task", is seven lines:

  > Create a Project and Session. Enter a focused scientific question, such as "Summarize the current research objective and propose the next analysis steps." To analyze local material, upload a CSV or PDF that you are authorized to use […] Review and approve the permission card […] Inspect tool calls and execution results in the message timeline.

  No dataset, no concrete prompt worth typing, no description of what the reader should end up looking at.
- "Next steps" links to deployment, configuration, runtime behavior, built-in tools, and architecture — all reference and explanation material. **There is no next tutorial to go to.**
- The only end-to-end walkthrough in the repo, `how-to/literature-research-case-guide.md` (212 lines), is filed under how-to and covers a single domain. Nothing in the tutorial points to it.
- **11 of the 18 skills shipped in `skills/` are not mentioned anywhere in `docs/`** (checked case-insensitively, including spaced forms): `assessment-screening`, `citation-reviewer`, `code-engineer`, `computation-reviewer`, `creative-material-design`, `evidence-extractor`, `insight-aggregator`, `literature-searcher`, `report-writer`, `result-evaluator`, `science-research-team`. A new user cannot discover that `literature-searcher` or `report-writer` exists, let alone how to drive them.

## Why this matters

A tutorial's job is to walk someone to their first success. Today the path ends at "enter a focused scientific question" — the reader is handed a blank box immediately after paying the setup cost. [#22](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/22) reported this same class of problem from a real 0.2.0 trial: the user got through the interface but never reached the product's value.

The reference material is genuinely thorough (`rest-api`, `configuration`, `builtin-tools`, `runtime-behavior`). The missing piece is the learning path, not the specification.

## Proposal

### A. Finish the tutorial series

Numbered pages, each completable in ~15 minutes, each ending with something the reader can point at:

1. **`01-quick-start.md`** — keep, but replace §4 with one concrete first task: a named input, the exact prompt, and a description of the result.
2. **`02-analyze-a-dataset.md`** — upload a small CSV, ask a question, approve the first code-execution permission card, read the resulting chart or table, find it in the Artifact area.
3. **`03-literature-search-and-report.md`** — `literature-searcher` → `evidence-extractor` → `report-writer`, ending in a cited report. The existing 212-line case guide is good source material, trimmed to tutorial length.
4. **`04-use-and-write-skills.md`** — enable a bundled skill, then build one with `skill-creator`.
5. **`05-connect-a-tool.md`** — add an MCP connector and use it in a session. `how-to/configure-custom-mcp.md` covers the settings screen; the tutorial covers the round trip.
6. **`06-trace-a-result.md`** — approvals, provenance, and where a conclusion's evidence lives (pairs with `explanation/review-provenance.md`, and with ScienceMemory where enabled).

### B. Add quick-start case examples

Short, self-contained, copy-pasteable. Each case states: the input file, the prompt to type, what the reader should see, roughly how long it takes, and which skills/connectors it needs. Ideally shipped with a tiny sample dataset — the repository currently has no `examples/` or sample-data directory, so every walkthrough starts by asking the reader to supply their own file.

The current quick start rightly notes that outputs "are not fixed-output promises" since they depend on the model. Tutorials should therefore describe the **shape** of the expected result ("a chart appears in the Artifact panel; the timeline shows a code execution you approved") rather than promising exact text.

### C. Make the bundled skills discoverable

A `reference/skills.md`, or a tutorial appendix, listing all 18 skills in `skills/`: what each does, when to enable it, and which tutorial exercises it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `docs/en/tutorial/` and `docs/zh/tutorial/` contain more than one page, and each page links to the next.
- [ ] Every tutorial states a concrete input, the prompt to type, and what the reader should see.
- [ ] At least one tutorial runs end to end on a sample file shipped in the repository.
- [ ] Every bundled skill is named in at least one document.
- [ ] `01-quick-start.md` ends by pointing at the next tutorial, not only at reference pages.
- [ ] English and Chinese versions land together.

## Open questions

- Which domain should the flagship case be: general CSV analysis, or the literature survey that already has a case guide?
- Can a small, license-clean sample dataset be committed for tutorial use?
- Should tutorials assume the prepackaged binary (the README's primary path) and mention source/Docker only in passing?
- Screenshots: worth the maintenance cost? `docs/images/` already holds 15 UI captures, so the precedent exists.

Related: [#25](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/25) covers building and publishing the docs site and completing the reference/explanation gaps; this issue is specifically the tutorial and case-example side.

## Summary

The README is the first and often only page a visitor reads, and right now it does not do the three jobs it should: **say clearly what this is and who it is for, summarize the core capabilities in a scannable form, and hand the reader a path into the tutorials.** I would like it reworked around those three.

## Current state

`README.md` and `README_zh.md` are 57 lines each: intro sentence → security warning → Project positioning → Features → Related documents → Requirements → Installation → Quick start → License.

Concrete problems:

1. **The pitch is one sentence, and the second thing a visitor reads is a disclaimer.** Line 3 carries the whole value proposition; lines 7–8 are a `[!WARNING]` block about loopback binding, bearer tokens, TLS termination, and sandbox boundaries. That warning is correct and should stay in the README — but placing it above everything else means a first-time reader meets the caveats before they have any idea what the product does.

2. **"Project positioning" does not describe positioning, and the two languages disagree.** The English section is an architecture paragraph ("A browser UI communicates with a Node control API. Each agent run is driven by a Python Gateway…"). The Chinese section at the same position is a **verbatim copy of the intro sentence at line 12**. So one language repeats itself and the other answers a different question entirely.

3. **The feature list is dense prose with no links and an unsourced number.** Four bullets, each a 2–3 line paragraph. None of them links to anything — not a doc, not a tutorial, not a screenshot. The claim "over 300 cross-domain Skills" appears **only in the two READMEs and nowhere else in the repository or docs**, while `skills/` ships 18. Whatever the 300 refers to, a reader cannot verify it or find out how to reach those skills.

4. **No visuals at all.** Both READMEs contain zero images (`grep -c '!\['` → 0), while `docs/images/` already holds 15 UI captures — `project.png`, `task.png`, `model.png`, `skill.png`, `connector.png`, `permission.png`, `memory.png`, `quotas.png`, `evidence1–4.jpg`, and more. A product whose pitch is "watch the whole research workflow and trace every deliverable" shows the reader nothing.

5. **Exactly one tutorial link, buried at line 51 of 57**, mid-paragraph, after a `curl` health check. Nothing in the Features section points at how to actually try any of those features.

6. **The Installation section is a stub.** In full: "Prepare a ScienceDiscovery executable for the host architecture. Binary packaging, source mode, and Docker procedures are documented in the deployment guide." It never says where to get an executable — which is precisely what [#1](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/1) asked.

## Proposal

Restructure both READMEs to this order:

1. **Title + one-line pitch + badges.** One sentence a researcher recognizes themselves in. Keep the existing positioning sentence if it tests well; just make it the hero line, not a paragraph competing with three other paragraphs.
2. **One screenshot or short GIF** of a real session — timeline, a generated artifact, the provenance view. Reuse what is already in `docs/images/`.
3. **"What you can do with it" — a scannable feature table**, one row per capability, each row linking to the tutorial or how-to that exercises it. Sketch:

   | Capability | What it means | Try it |
   |---|---|---|
   | Literature and data connectors | One-click access to paper and data repositories | `how-to/configure-custom-mcp.md`, literature tutorial |
   | Sandboxed code execution | Agents write and run Python/R/shell in a fail-closed sandbox | dataset-analysis tutorial |
   | Task decomposition and skills | Complex tasks broken down and dispatched across skills | skills tutorial |
   | Full-chain traceability | Code, environment, logs, and evidence for every deliverable | `explanation/review-provenance.md`, tracing tutorial |

   The "Try it" column is the part that matters: every claim becomes something the reader can go do. The tutorial targets come from [#26](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/26); until those pages exist, the column points at the pages that do.
4. **Get started in three steps** — download, run, first task — with a real download location, then straight into the quick-start tutorial.
5. **Then** requirements, deployment paths, the security warning, contributing, and license. Keep the warning prominent and unsoftened, just below the getting-started path rather than above the pitch.

Also: either source the "300+ Skills" claim (link to wherever that library lives) or restate it in terms a reader can check.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A visitor can tell within the first screen what the product does, for whom, and what it costs them to try.
- [ ] Every feature claim links to a page that demonstrates or documents it.
- [ ] At least one screenshot or GIF of the product appears above the fold.
- [ ] The tutorial entry point is a prominent link, not a clause in a paragraph.
- [ ] "Installation" says where to obtain a binary.
- [ ] The security warning is still present and unsoftened.
- [ ] `README.md` and `README_zh.md` have the same structure and make the same claims; the Chinese "项目定位" section no longer duplicates the intro verbatim.
- [ ] The "300+ Skills" figure is sourced or restated.

## Open questions

- Is there a public download or release page the README can link to, or is distribution internal for now?
- Screenshot or animated GIF — and can one be captured from a build that is safe to publish (no tokens, no internal hostnames)?
- What does the "300+ Skills" number count?
- Should the README carry the feature table, or stay short and delegate to a docs landing page once [#25](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/25) publishes one?

Related: [#25](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/25) (docs site + content completeness), [#26](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/26) (tutorial series), [#22](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/22) (onboarding experience), [#1](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/1) (finding the download).

## Summary

When a dependency is missing, `scripts/start-stack.sh` prints one sentence naming the requirement and exits. It never says how to satisfy it or where to read more, so the first thing a new user meets is a dead end.

## Current behaviour

`scripts/start-stack.sh` (lines 212–250):

```bash
require_command() { # <command> <failure message>
  command -v "$1" >/dev/null || { echo "$2" >&2; exit 1; }
}

require_command node   "Node.js 22.19+ is required."
require_command pnpm   "pnpm 11.1.2 is required."
require_command python3 "Python 3 is required for workspace analysis."
require_command uv     "uv 0.9+ is required for the Python service environments."
require_command curl   "curl is required for local service startup checks."
require_command "${SCIENCE_AGENT_BWRAP_PATH:-bwrap}" "bubblewrap is required for isolated Linux execution."
require_command "${SCIENCE_AGENT_SEATBELT_PATH:-/usr/bin/sandbox-exec}" "macOS sandbox-exec is required for isolated execution."
```

So on a fresh machine the entire output is:

```
pnpm 11.1.2 is required.
```

and the process exits 1.

One check already does better and is worth copying — the Node version gate reports what it found:

```
Node.js 22.19+ is required; found v20.11.0.
```

That is the right shape; it is just missing the "and here is how to fix it" half, and the other seven checks do not even report the found version.

## Why this matters

The target audience is researchers, not Node developers. "pnpm 11.1.2 is required" assumes the reader knows what pnpm is, that it is installed through corepack or npm, and that the version is pinned deliberately. `uv` and `bubblewrap` are worse — neither is something a scientist would have encountered, and `bwrap` is not even the name printed in the error, so searching for "bubblewrap" and searching for the binary give different results.

The information exists: `README.md` has a requirements table, and `docs/*/how-to/deployment.md` has per-platform install commands. The failure message just never points there. This is the same class of stumble reported in [#22](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/22) — the product is reachable but the path to it is not explained.

## Proposal

Extend `require_command` to take a remedy, and print three things on failure: what is missing, what was found (when anything was), and one concrete next step.

```
uv 0.9+ is required for the Python service environments; not found on PATH.
Install:  curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
Details:  docs/en/how-to/deployment.md#local-mode-host-processes
```

Specifically:

- **node / pnpm** — name the version manager the project expects (corepack, `npm i -g pnpm@11.1.2`, or whatever is canonical here) rather than leaving the reader to pick.
- **uv** — the official install line, plus the note that it is only needed for source mode.
- **bubblewrap** — the package name per distro (`apt install bubblewrap`, `dnf install bubblewrap`) and the fact that the binary is `bwrap`, since the error names one and `command -v` looks for the other.
- **sandbox-exec** — say it ships with macOS, so "missing" almost always means a restricted parent sandbox rather than something to install; `docs/en/how-to/deployment.md` already explains this, and the error should link to it.
- Report the found version wherever a version gate exists, as the Node check already does.
- Collect all failures before exiting instead of stopping at the first one, so a user on a bare machine learns everything they need in one run rather than in five.

Keep each message to two or three lines — this is not a place for a wall of text.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every preflight failure names the missing dependency, what was found (if anything), and a concrete install step or doc link.
- [ ] The doc link resolves to a section that actually covers that dependency.
- [ ] The bubblewrap message reconciles the package name with the `bwrap` binary name.
- [ ] A machine missing several dependencies reports them all in one run.
- [ ] The messages stay short enough to read in a terminal.

## Open question

Should the install commands live in the script, or should the script print only a doc anchor and keep the platform-specific commands in the deployment guide? Inline commands are more immediately useful; a single doc anchor is easier to keep correct.
oldest.title: [Feature]: Dependency preflight failures should say how to fix them, not just what is missing

oldest.body:
## Summary

ScienceDiscovery ships a real command-line client — `ScienceDiscovery run` — that can drive a full agent task, stream JSONL, read from stdin, and be scripted. **The README never mentions it in either language.** A researcher who wants to batch a hundred runs from a job script has no way to learn the capability exists short of running `help`.

## What already exists

From `services/launcher/src/cli-options.ts` (the binary's own `help` output):

```text
Commands:
  serve                    Start the Web UI, control API and sandbox runner
  run [input] [options]    Run an agent task via a running serve (CLI client)
  extract --to <dir>       Unpack the embedded runtime payload without starting it
  version                  Print the release version and bundled runtime versions
  help                     Show this message
```

`run` takes 13 options: `--content`, `--stdin`, `--session`, `--project`, `--model`, `--skills`, `--connectors`, `--approval`, `--auto-approve`, `--review`, `--token`, `--output <jsonl|text>`, `--timeout`.

`services/launcher/src/run.ts` documents the behaviour that makes it scriptable:

- **text mode** (default on a TTY): the answer streams to stdout, status and progress to stderr — so `run "question" > answer.md` yields a clean file.
- **jsonl mode** (default when piped): every event is one JSON line on stdout, errors included, so a downstream `jq` never meets a non-JSON line.

This is a genuinely useful capability for the target audience: reproducible batch runs from a job script, a run per dataset, output piped straight into an analysis pipeline.

## The gap

1. **Neither README mentions it.** `README.md` and `README_zh.md` contain no occurrence of "CLI", "command line", "命令行", "headless", `jsonl`, or `ScienceDiscovery run`. Quick start shows only `./ScienceDiscovery serve`.

2. **The English deployment guide omits the command entirely.** The two guides disagree:

   | Guide | Commands listed |
   |---|---|
   | `docs/zh/how-to/deployment.md` | `serve`, **`run`**, `extract`, `version`, `help` |
   | `docs/en/how-to/deployment.md` | `serve`, `extract`, `version`, `help` |

   The Chinese guide also carries a worked example and the mode/approval rules; the English guide has none of it. So today the CLI is documented **only in Chinese**.

3. There is no `reference/cli.md` in either language — raised separately in [#25](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/25).

## Proposal

Add a short **Command line** section to `README.md` and `README_zh.md`, after Quick start — four or five lines, not a manual:

````markdown
## Command line

Besides the Web UI, a running `serve` can be driven from the terminal:

```bash
./ScienceDiscovery serve &                      # start the stack
./ScienceDiscovery run "Summarize these results" > answer.md
cat prompt.txt | ./ScienceDiscovery run --stdin --auto-approve | jq .
```

`run` connects to the same control plane as the browser and reads the token
from the data directory, so no extra setup is needed when `run` and `serve`
share a `--data-dir`. On a TTY the answer goes to stdout and progress to
stderr; when piped it emits JSONL, and a non-interactive run must pass
`--auto-approve` because it cannot answer permission prompts.
See [CLI reference](docs/en/reference/cli.md) for every command and option.
````

And alongside it:

- Add `run` to the command list in `docs/en/how-to/deployment.md` so the two languages match, porting the example and the text/jsonl and approval rules from the Chinese guide.
- If the README grows a feature table ([#27](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/27)), give scripted/batch use a row of its own — it is a differentiator worth stating, not a footnote.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both READMEs introduce the CLI with at least one runnable example.
- [ ] The README states the TTY/pipe output-mode difference and the `--auto-approve` requirement for non-interactive runs, so a first scripted attempt does not fail unexplained.
- [ ] `docs/en/how-to/deployment.md` lists `run` alongside `serve`, `extract`, `version`, and `help`.
- [ ] The English and Chinese command lists match.
- [ ] The README links to a CLI reference once one exists.

## Open questions

- Does the README keep a short teaser and delegate details to the deployment guide / CLI reference, or carry a slightly fuller example?
- Should the example use the binary (`./ScienceDiscovery run`) only, or also show the source-mode equivalent?

Related: [#25](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/25) (a `reference/cli.md` and the docs site), [#27](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/27) (README rework).

## Summary

ScienceDiscovery cannot run on Windows in any form. The word "windows" does not appear in `README.md` or in either deployment guide — it is not a documented limitation, it is simply absent. Comparable open-source research workbenches ship Windows desktop builds, so this excludes a large share of the researchers we are aiming at.

## What blocks Windows today

| Layer | Current state |
|---|---|
| Sandbox | `SandboxProvider = "bubblewrap" \| "seatbelt"` (`packages/sandbox-capability/src/index.ts:34`). No Windows provider exists. |
| Platform branch | `services/launcher/src/serve.ts:213`: `process.platform === "darwin" ? "darwin" : "linux"` — everything non-macOS is assumed Linux. |
| Shell | `packages/executor/src/environment.ts:85` hardcodes `/bin/bash` (macOS) or `/usr/bin/bash` (Linux). |
| Binary packaging | `scripts/package-binary-release.sh:131` emits `ScienceDiscovery-<version>-linux-<arch>` only. |
| Startup script | `scripts/start-stack.sh` is bash, and its `uname -s` switch exits with "Native sandbox execution is unsupported on …" for anything but Darwin/Linux. |
| Runner SEA | Linux x64/arm64 only. |
| Docker path | README marks it Linux-only (needs host unprivileged user namespaces). |

The crux is the sandbox. Code execution is deliberately fail-closed, and there is no Windows equivalent of Bubblewrap, so Windows support is a sandbox question first and a packaging question second. `--skip-sandbox-check` must **not** become the Windows story: shipping a platform where `run_shell` executes unsandboxed would quietly break the security contract the README states.

## Proposal

Treat this as two tracks with very different costs.

### Track A — a supported WSL2 path (small, do this first)

WSL2 is a real Linux kernel with user namespaces, so Bubblewrap works there. Most of the work is verification and documentation rather than code:

- Test the binary and source mode under WSL2 (Ubuntu), including Bubblewrap with unprivileged user namespaces.
- Make preflight detect WSL and give WSL-specific guidance instead of generic Linux text.
- Document the path in the deployment guide: which distro, how to reach the UI from the Windows browser (WSL2 forwards `localhost` by default), where the data directory lives, and the performance caveat about working under `/mnt/c` versus the Linux filesystem.
- Mention Docker Desktop with the WSL2 backend as the second option, and state whether the unprivileged-userns requirement holds inside that VM.

This unblocks Windows users in days, not months, and costs no new sandbox code.

### Track B — native Windows (large, needs a design first)

Requires, at minimum:

- A Windows sandbox provider. Candidates: AppContainer plus a restricted token and Job Objects (in-process, no extra install, weaker than Bubblewrap); Windows Sandbox (strong, but Pro/Enterprise only and heavyweight per-execution); a Hyper-V utility VM. Each needs its own threat-model write-up against what Bubblewrap currently guarantees.
- Replacing the hardcoded bash execution path with a platform-aware shell spec.
- Windows path handling across workspaces, CAS, and the data directory.
- A win32 SEA for the runner and a Windows packaging target.
- A decision on what `scientific_capability`/micromamba provisioning means on Windows.

This should start as an RFC that states which sandbox guarantees survive, not as an implementation PR.

## Acceptance criteria

**Track A**
- [ ] The deployment guide has a tested WSL2 section (EN + ZH).
- [ ] Preflight recognizes WSL and prints WSL-appropriate remediation.
- [ ] A WSL2 run passes the same sandbox probe as native Linux, or the difference is documented.
- [ ] The README's requirements table names Windows explicitly — supported via WSL2 — instead of staying silent.

**Track B**
- [ ] A design document states the Windows sandbox provider and how its guarantees compare to Bubblewrap.
- [ ] No Windows path ships that runs user code outside a sandbox by default.

## Open questions

- Is Windows in scope for the product at all, or is the intended answer "use WSL2"? Either is fine — but the README should say which.
- If native Windows is in scope, which sandbox primitive is acceptable to the security review?
- Does the Ascend NPU path have any Windows story, or is remote compute the answer there?
oldest.title: [Feature]: Support Windows — a tested WSL2 path now, native Windows as a design question

## Summary

There is no update mechanism of any kind: `autoUpdate` / `checkForUpdate` appear nowhere in the codebase. A user who installed a binary months ago has no way to learn that a newer release exists, short of visiting the repository. Comparable workbenches ship auto-updating desktop builds; we do not even notify.

## Current state

- **Version is visible, staleness is not.** `ScienceDiscovery version` prints the release version plus bundled Node/CPython/micromamba versions. Nothing ever compares that against what has since been published.
- **Releases already carry the right metadata.** `scripts/package-binary-release.sh` emits `VERSION` and `SHA256SUMS` next to the artifacts, and the binary-release flow already verifies downloads by pinned SHA-256 (that is how Node, CPython, micromamba, and the uv wheel are fetched). The building blocks for a verifiable update check exist.
- **Side-by-side versions already work.** The payload cache is digest-keyed (`~/.cache/science-discovery/payload/<payload-id>`) and "an upgrade does not overwrite an older extraction", so an older release stays runnable — rollback is feasible today.
- **Remote runners can silently drift.** The Runner SEA is versioned by the build's Git commit prefix, and a mismatch between the local control plane and an already-deployed remote runner only produces a warning; it does not block or redeploy. So a long-lived SSH target can keep running a months-old runner.
- **No documented upgrade contract.** There is no guide covering data-directory compatibility across releases, what a new binary rebuilds on first `serve`, or how to roll back (also noted in [#25](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/25)).

## Proposal

### 1. Update check (the part that matters most)

An opt-in check against a published release manifest — the existing `VERSION` + `SHA256SUMS` pair is already close to one.

- **Off by default in air-gapped installs**, and settable in system configuration. No telemetry beyond fetching the manifest; do not send an install identifier.
- Route the request through the configured network proxy, since proxy settings already exist.
- Surface the result quietly: a dismissible banner in the UI, a line in `ScienceDiscovery version`, and an explicit `--check-updates` for scripts.
- Fail silent on a network error. An offline workstation must never see an error toast because an update check could not reach the internet.

### 2. Self-update (optional second step)

`ScienceDiscovery update` that downloads the new artifact, verifies it against `SHA256SUMS` (ideally a signature too), swaps it atomically, and keeps the previous binary so a rollback is one command. The digest-keyed payload cache means the old version's extracted runtime is still there.

For Docker and source mode, print the right command instead of attempting anything — `docker compose pull` / `git pull && ./scripts/start-stack.sh` — rather than pretending a binary self-update applies.

### 3. Upgrade contract

Document, and enforce in code:

- what the data directory guarantees across versions, and what the first `serve` after an upgrade rebuilds;
- refusing to open a data directory written by a newer release, rather than half-migrating it;
- redeploying the matching Runner SEA to remote hosts when the control plane updates, instead of only warning about the mismatch.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user on an outdated release is told so, in the UI and on the CLI.
- [ ] The check is opt-in/opt-out, proxy-aware, and silent on failure.
- [ ] No update path installs an artifact whose SHA-256 was not verified.
- [ ] Rollback to the previous version is documented and works.
- [ ] Docker and source-mode users get correct upgrade instructions rather than a binary self-update.
- [ ] Remote runner drift is resolved automatically or reported as an actionable error.

## Open questions

- Where would the release manifest live, given the canonical repository is on GitCode and GitHub is a mirror? It needs one stable URL.
- Should releases be signed, or is SHA-256 against a manifest over HTTPS sufficient for this threat model?
- Default for the update check on a fresh install: on or off?
oldest.title: [Feature]: Notify users of new releases, and support self-update
oldest.author: Birfy

items.body:
### 🚀 Background Description


ScienceDiscovery contains maintained Python services whose tests are not represented by the Node.js coverage percentage. A Node-only number must not be presented as whole-repository coverage.

This issue adds a separate Python coverage pipeline using mature Python tooling. It complements the Node.js coverage issue #137 while keeping the two languages' commands, reports, and scope independently auditable.

### Design Ideas

### Measurement

- Use `coverage.py` as the coverage engine; do not implement a custom Python tracer.
- Preserve existing test frameworks:
  - `services/gateway` and `services/paper`: `unittest`
  - `services/memory-graph` and `services/evolve`: `pytest`
- Run each existing suite under `coverage run --branch --parallel-mode`, then use `coverage combine`.
- Measure production source directories, not test files.
- Record covered/total counts and percentages for lines and branches. Keep service/path groups separate.

### CI execution

- Reuse existing CI and nightly workflows rather than adding a standalone coverage workflow.
- PR/default-branch runs should select affected Python services where the dependency/selector mapping is reliable. A partial run must be explicitly marked partial and must never be displayed as whole-Python coverage.
- The existing nightly run should execute the complete Python coverage scope and publish the authoritative baseline.
- Coverage remains informational initially; existing test failures still fail the job.

### Reports and artifact

- Generate `coverage.py` JSON as the structured source consumed by the board.
- Optionally generate Cobertura XML for future GitHub Code Quality integration and LCOV/HTML for local diagnosis, without making a paid GitHub feature a prerequisite.
- Upload one SHA-qualified Actions artifact containing aggregate and per-service JSON summaries plus run identity metadata.
- Use repository default artifact retention.

### Dashboard

- Display Node.js and Python coverage as separate first-class metrics.
- If an overall line percentage is shown, compute it from summed covered/total lines:
  `(node covered + python covered) / (node total + python total)`.
- Never average percentages directly.
- Label nightly baselines as authoritative and partial/incremental results explicitly.

### Involved Public APIs

No product runtime or public API changes are proposed.

This feature adds an internal Python coverage artifact contract. It should align with the Node summary's run/SHA/mode/group metadata while retaining Python-specific metrics and source paths.

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- `services/gateway` and `services/paper` keep their existing `unittest` commands.
- `services/memory-graph` and `services/evolve` keep their existing `pytest` commands and extras.
- CI test selection and nightly scheduling determine whether the result is partial or authoritative.
- The status board consumes the structured Actions artifact; it does not run Python tests itself.
- GitHub Code Quality can consume Cobertura XML later, but this feature must work without enabling the paid service.

### Test Design and Test Plan

- Add focused coverage runs for every maintained Python service and verify existing tests still execute with the same pass/fail semantics.
- Test combining parallel coverage data from `unittest` and `pytest` environments.
- Verify branch coverage is enabled and test files are excluded from production totals.
- Verify missing/failed service runs cannot produce an authoritative aggregate.
- Verify partial PR results and complete nightly baselines have distinct metadata.
- Validate JSON totals against `coverage report` for representative services.
- Add board parser/rendering tests for Python-only, Node-only, combined, missing, and stale artifacts.
- Verify overall coverage uses summed covered/total values, not the arithmetic mean of percentages.
- Run the complete repository test suite before merging.

### Additional Information

Related work:

- Node.js coverage tracking: #137
- Node.js WIP implementation: #134
- Companion status-board PR: https://github.com/ScienceDiscovery/github-status-board/pull/1
- coverage.py documentation: https://coverage.readthedocs.io/

Non-goals: migrating all Python tests to one framework, implementing a custom coverage engine, or requiring GitHub Code Quality/another paid service.
items.title: [Feature]: Add Python test coverage collection and dashboard reporting
items.author: wyhohyw

items.body:
### 🚀 Background Description


ScienceDiscovery runs Node.js tests in CI but does not yet publish a durable, machine-readable coverage result tied to the exact workflow run and commit. Maintainers should be able to inspect coverage in GitHub Actions, while the status board should consume the same CI evidence without running tests itself or parsing unstable console text.

This issue covers **Node.js coverage only**. Python coverage should be tracked separately so that the tools, test commands, scope, and percentages remain explicit.

The current work-in-progress implementation is PR #134.

### Design Ideas

### Measurement

- Reuse the repository's existing built Node.js tests; do not introduce another test tier or migrate test frameworks.
- Run them with Node.js 22's built-in `--experimental-test-coverage` collector (V8 coverage).
- Group results by workspace/path and keep repository CI-script tests as explicit groups.
- Exclude test sources from production-source totals.
- Record covered/total counts and percentages for lines, branches, and functions rather than storing percentages alone.

### CI execution

- Integrate coverage into the existing `.github/workflows/ci.yml`; do not add a second coverage workflow.
- For pull requests and default-branch pushes, select changed Node.js workspaces and their transitive dependents. Changes to shared coverage infrastructure select every group.
- Reuse the existing nightly workflow for a complete, authoritative all-group baseline.
- Skip coverage for release-only calls.
- Test failures still fail the job. Coverage percentages are informational initially and do not introduce a new threshold gate.

### Actions artifact

- Generate LCOV only as a local intermediate.
- Upload one SHA-qualified artifact containing aggregate and per-group JSON summaries.
- Include source SHA, base SHA, generation time, mode (`incremental` or `full`), selected groups, and whether the result is authoritative.
- Use the repository's default artifact retention; do not introduce independent 30/90-day policies.

### Status-board consumption

- The board downloads the structured summary through the GitHub Actions Artifacts API. It does not execute tests and does not infer coverage from log text.
- Show the latest full nightly baseline, per-path line/branch/function coverage, nightly history, and recent PR affected-group results.
- A homepage value composed from later default-branch group summaries must be labelled as an estimate until the next full nightly run recalibrates it.

### Involved Public APIs

No product runtime or public API changes are proposed.

The feature adds an internal CI artifact contract for coverage summaries. Consumers must treat the run identity, SHA, mode, selected groups, and authoritative flag as part of that contract.

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- Existing CI and nightly workflows provide the execution environment.
- Existing Node workspace dependency metadata is used to expand changed workspaces to transitive dependents.
- The companion status board reads the Actions artifact and renders the coverage page.
- Browser/TSX, Python, and Playwright coverage are explicitly excluded from this issue and must not be represented as covered by the Node percentage.
- GitHub Code Quality/Cobertura upload can be evaluated separately; it is not required for the initial board integration.

### Test Design and Test Plan

- Add selector tests for changed workspaces, transitive dependents, shared-infrastructure full selection, and irrelevant-path skips.
- Add aggregation tests that exclude test sources and preserve aggregate and per-group covered/total values.
- Validate that PR/default-branch CI publishes affected-group summaries from the existing CI workflow.
- Validate that nightly publishes a complete authoritative baseline without a second workflow.
- Verify that every artifact is tied to its workflow run/SHA and contains only the structured JSON required by consumers.
- Verify that test failures still fail the coverage job.
- Add status-board tests distinguishing authoritative nightly data, incremental/PR data, estimates, and UT/ST/E2E artifacts.
- Run the repository's complete existing test suite before merging.

### Additional Information

Related work:

- WIP implementation: #134
- Companion status-board PR: https://github.com/ScienceDiscovery/github-status-board/pull/1
- Design in the implementation branch: `docs/designs/test-coverage.v3.md`

Acceptance boundary: the resulting percentage covers built Node.js workspace tests and repository CI-script tests only. It must never be presented as whole-repository coverage.

items.body:
## Problem and intended outcome

Developers cannot reliably answer “which command runs this test?” or “did this invocation cover all selected tests?” The repository has overlapping entry points, inconsistent discovery rules, and test assets that are not represented in the shared catalog.

Consolidate test discovery and execution around the existing catalog so that local development and CI use the same selection logic. Every maintained test asset should have an identifiable owner and execution entry point, and a successful command must not conceal missing, unsupported, or unexecuted tests.

This is a focused implementation issue derived from [GitCode RFC #107: UT, ST and E2E test coverage and engineering](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/107). That is a GitCode issue, not GitHub issue #107.

## Evidence from the current branch

Inspected branch: `feat/jiuwenswarm`, commit [`57ff5f48802d4c495d10f01a2b211fccfdeb62ae`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/tree/57ff5f48802d4c495d10f01a2b211fccfdeb62ae). These observations describe this revision, not necessarily the current default branch.

- Root `pnpm test`, `pnpm check`, and `pnpm ci:ut` execute different combinations. Root `test` builds, runs binary-script tests, and invokes workspace package tests; it does not mean all Python, ST, and E2E tests ran.
- `.ci/test-catalog.mjs` registers eight aggregate tasks. The seven standalone `test/api/*journey.mjs` drivers, `test/contract` scenarios/tooling tests, and the new Python adapter suite are not fully represented in the shared execution path.
- `test/playwright.config.ts` scans the entire `test/` directory without an explicit browser-only `testMatch`. During the preceding E2E assessment, Playwright discovery also triggered TAP output from the contract tooling's `node:test` files.
- Node package scripts enumerate different glob depths. Web currently includes both `tests/*.test.ts` and `tests/*.test.tsx`, but does not recursively discover subdirectories. The RFC's earlier missing-`.test.ts` observation must not be reapplied as an unresolved fact on this branch.
- Some API journey drivers construct their own environment and start the native executor. Setting an outer JiuwenSwarm environment variable does not make those drivers validate JiuwenSwarm.
- Existing catalog and E2E metadata checks pass despite these gaps. Entry-point consistency checks alone do not prove that all test assets are collected.

Relevant files: root `package.json`, `.ci/test-catalog.mjs`, `.ci/test-selector.mjs`, `.ci/ci-contract.mjs`, `.ci/run-e2e.sh`, `apps/web/package.json`, `test/playwright.config.ts`, and `test/check-e2e-meta.mjs`.

## Proposed scope

### 1. Load adjacent test configuration through the existing catalog

Do not create a competing registry or replace the existing test frameworks.

- Register module tests as suites with explicit discovery rules; do not manually enumerate thousands of unit-test cases.
- Give important ST and E2E journeys stable case IDs for individual selection and reporting.
- Include standalone journey/smoke drivers, JSON contract scenarios, Python suites, and test-tooling self-tests, not just files named `*.test.*` or `*.spec.*`.
- Describe source, runner, owner, layer, capabilities, environment requirements, timeout, gates, and supported executors where applicable.
- Keep model mode, sandbox/hardware requirements, and executor support independent of the test layer.
- Store scenario metadata in adjacent versioned `*.case.yaml` files and module discovery rules in `*.suite.yaml` files. The existing catalog loads these configurations; it is not a second manually maintained registry.
- Use `llm.mode: none | stub | real | unreviewed`, separate `supportedExecutors` from `ci.pr.executors` / `ci.daily.executors`, and declare `required` per CI policy. A nonblocking policy requires a reason and must retain its actual failures/blockers.
- Preserve narrative E2E-META comments for purpose, steps and dependencies; use YAML as the authority for machine-readable classification and policy.

The catalog can initially remain at `.ci/test-catalog.mjs`. A later move to `test/catalog.mjs` should retain a compatibility export rather than two independently maintained definitions.

### 2. Provide one documented command interface

Shared command interface (install dependencies with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` first):

```bash
pnpm test:list
pnpm test:doctor
pnpm test:check
pnpm test:pr
pnpm test:daily
pnpm test --profile local
pnpm test --layer st --capability permission
pnpm test --layer e2e --surface browser --executor jiuwenswarm
pnpm test --case st.api.child-workspace --executor native
pnpm test --profile full --executor both
```

Existing `ci:*` commands should remain compatible wrappers over the shared selector/runner. Document precisely what the default profile includes; do not silently reduce existing coverage when changing `pnpm test`.

A full selection must show gated real-model, hardware, and legacy tasks as blocked when prerequisites or opt-ins are absent. Listing must not execute test bodies or contact live model endpoints. Distinguish static asset inventory from framework-expanded test counts.

### 3. Enforce complete, framework-specific discovery

- Recursively enumerate Node/Web test files and pass explicit file arguments to the runner, avoiding shell-dependent glob depth.
- Check source-to-build test mapping so stale `dist` files cannot keep deleted tests alive.
- Restrict Playwright to the browser journey directory and an explicit `**/*.spec.ts` pattern.
- Preserve Python runner discovery semantics and explicitly identify tests requiring live dependencies.
- Fail asset validation for unowned files, stale catalog/quarantine entries, unintended duplicate ownership, and unknown case IDs.
- Treat unexpected empty selections as an error, not a successful run.

Keep module tests near their modules. Separate cross-module assets into `test/st/`, `test/e2e/`, `test/st/api/`, and, where appropriate, `test/st/local-stack/`. Test helpers and their own unit tests must not be collected as browser journeys. A broader domain-by-domain directory reorganization is not required for this issue.

### 4. Make selected scope and execution results explicit

Record the selected suites/cases, actual runner and executor, revision, outcomes, reasons, and evidence locations. Distinguish `PASS`, `FAIL`, `BLOCKED`, `SKIPPED`, and `NOT_RUN`; retain retry history instead of hiding instability.

An executor-specific selection must never silently fall back to another executor. Existing native-only drivers should declare that limitation until they support JiuwenSwarm. Executor-independent tests need not run twice.

Full assessment mode should continue independent suites after a failure and still return a failing result. Preserve fail-fast as an explicit option. A zero process exit code alone is insufficient evidence when the selected cases or required contract assertions were not executed.

## Suggested delivery sequence

1. Inventory existing assets and extend catalog/validation coverage while keeping existing paths and commands operational.
2. Introduce shared selection/discovery and targeted directory separation. Update imports, root calculations, metadata checks, CI paths/cache keys, documentation, and the E2E skill together.
3. Route local and CI entry points through the shared implementation and normalize selection/results reporting.

Keep product fixes separate. The agreed scope now also includes case-configured subject models and deterministic/LLM/hybrid assertions, with the original framework checks retained. Two obsolete browser declarations were subsequently approved for retirement: the unconditional persistent-kernel teardown placeholder and the fixme for the removed manual paper-search form. Record both original identities, reasons, replacement coverage or the remaining coverage gap in the migration record. Rename issue-number filenames by scenario/object. Preserve a before/after mapping of all remaining identities, not just equal aggregate counts.

## Agreed directory and layer model

UT is colocated with its owning code; `test/support/` is implementation code for the test infrastructure, with its own adjacent UT. It is not a test layer.

```text
test/
  support/             # test infrastructure and colocated UT
    contract/          # shared replay, normalization and comparison code
  fixtures/            # shared data and stubs
  st/
    agent-runtime/     # cross-module agent collaboration
    api/               # backend HTTP/service-chain integration
    contract/          # HTTP/event-stream scenarios, baselines and policy
  e2e/                 # browser user journeys
```

Directly calling running backend services is ST for this browser-facing product. Both L1 HTTP contracts and L2 run-event contracts are ST; a longer backend flow does not make it a browser user E2E test. Contract tooling is shared once rather than copied between scenarios.

Case metadata and IDs follow these boundaries: `st.api.<scenario>` and `st.contract.<scenario>`, while browser IDs remain unchanged. The former draft paths/IDs are recorded in `test/support/migration.json` under `layoutMigration`. This move preserves all 92 configurations, their supported executors and PR/daily policies. `--layer e2e` now selects browser work only; `--layer st` includes API and contract scenarios.

## Scenario naming

Use lowercase kebab-case object/behavior names, without issue numbers, `journey-` / `-journey` or `l1-` / `l2-` labels. Examples:

- `test/e2e/first-run-onboarding.spec.ts` and `.case.yaml`, ID `e2e.browser.first-run-onboarding`.
- `test/st/api/child-workspace.mjs` and `.case.yaml`, ID `st.api.child-workspace`.
- `test/st/contract/cases/run-approval-denied.case.yaml`, scenario ID `run-approval-denied`, catalog ID `st.contract.run-approval-denied`.
- `session-multi-turn` describes the former `l2-two-turns` contract scenario; `run-events.json` holds run-event scenarios.

Implementation/config filenames and IDs stay aligned. Shared browser helpers are `scenario-fixtures.ts`, `scenario-report.ts` and `browser-fixture.ts`. Module UT follows module names; Python's conventional `test_*.py` discovery remains unchanged.

Step-report validation is now explicit in YAML (`reporting: steps`) rather than inferred from a `journey-` filename; all formerly marked journeys retain this enforcement. Naming validation rejects the historical test filename prefixes/suffixes.

`namingMigration` in `test/support/migration.json` records old/new paths, catalog IDs and contract scenario IDs. Baseline keys and accepted-difference case references are renamed together; expected response payloads, scenario steps and difference predicates are unchanged. External baselines using the old IDs need the same key migration. The naming migration preserved all 92 configured entries and their policies; the subsequent real-model extension below adds daily coverage, and all 88 retained browser test identities were verified after filename mapping.

## Test triggers and usage

| Trigger | Entry point and scope |
| --- | --- |
| Pull request opened, synchronized or reopened | `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: run `pnpm test:pr --layer ut`, `pnpm test:pr --layer st`, and the reusable `test-policy.yml` with `profile: pr`, `surface: browser`. Existing binary/Docker distribution gates remain. |
| Push to `main`/`master`, or manual dispatch of CI | Same PR policy and distribution jobs as above. Opening a PR into `feat/jiuwenswarm` also triggers the PR workflow; pushing only to an unrelated feature branch does not trigger the push rule. |
| Daily at 00:17 UTC / 08:17 Asia/Shanghai | `test-daily.yml` invokes the reusable workflow with `profile: daily`. GitHub scheduled workflows run from the default branch, so this starts only after the workflow reaches that branch. Manual `workflow_dispatch` is also declared, subject to GitHub workflow availability on the default branch. |
| Local PR/daily reproduction | `pnpm test:pr` / `pnpm test:daily` resolve the same YAML policy. Local callers must supply the required infrastructure; these commands do not reproduce all GitHub provisioning steps. |
| Explicit assessment | `pnpm test --profile full --executor both` selects all maintained scenario entries, including gated work. Unsupported/missing prerequisites are BLOCKED, not silently omitted. |

PR policy includes both UT tiers, native deterministic agent ST, and four JiuwenSwarm browser scenarios: first run, plugin composition, execution management and result delivery. Daily policy expands reviewed deterministic browser coverage to both executors and includes all seven native-only API journeys. After integration with target revision `9670568`, all 27 contract scenarios on two executor labels are observational because CI does not yet provision isolated contract targets or select the reviewed platform-specific comparison baseline. The target branch now includes `test/st/contract/baselines/legacy-linux.json` with L2 coverage. Real-model browser work now runs in the required daily real job; hardware and quarantined legacy work remain manual opt-ins.

```bash
# Inventory and inspect the exact policy without running test bodies.
pnpm test:list --profile pr --json
pnpm test:list --profile daily --json
pnpm test:doctor --case e2e.browser.first-run-onboarding --executor jiuwenswarm

# Run the configured policy or a selected scenario.
pnpm test:pr
pnpm test:daily
pnpm test --case e2e.browser.first-run-onboarding --executor jiuwenswarm
pnpm test --case st.api.child-workspace --executor native
pnpm test --profile full --executor both

# Validate configuration and test the harness itself.
pnpm test:check
pnpm test:tooling
pnpm ci:selftest
```

For JiuwenSwarm browser runs, provision an isolated instance (the GitHub reusable workflow calls `scripts/jiuwenswarm.sh setup/start/env`) and supply `JIUWENSWARM_GATEWAY_URL` and `JIUWENSWARM_MGMT_URL`. Formal browser/API runs require a built, committed candidate and isolated services. `test:doctor` reports declared prerequisites; READY is not a service health or product-pass certification.

Real model calls require `CI_ALLOW_REAL=1` and the named credentials/endpoints. Hardware, adapter-live, contract and legacy cases have their own explicit gates; selecting a profile never enables them. Contract replay additionally requires an isolated target, token, declared target executor and reviewed comparison baseline. An operator-declared executor label is not independent backend verification.

`required: true` outcomes fail the gate unless they pass. Observational failures/blockers remain visible and produce `passed-with-observations` when all required tasks pass. Full/manual assessment treats all selected entries as required. PR/daily executor matrices cannot be overridden by `--executor`; edit and review the YAML policy instead.

`pnpm test` retains its original build + binary tests + workspace-test scope; it does not mean all repository tests. Existing `ci:*` commands remain compatibility entry points, and CodeArts retains those commands' existing native scope. Reports are written below `.test-runs/` or `CI_RESULTS_DIR`, with selected IDs, configuration paths, revision, requested/actual executor, PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED/SKIPPED/NOT_RUN outcomes and command evidence. Static entry counts and framework-expanded test counts must be distinguished.

The implementation's `test/README.md` is the usage and configuration reference. New browser/API scenarios require adjacent case configuration; module unit tests inherit their suite entry point's policy. Unknown fields, duplicate IDs, missing sources, unsupported policy executors and unintended empty selections fail validation.

## Implementation and validation status

Implementation PR: [#129](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/129), with an additional commit aligning directories and YAML layers to the agreed UT/ST/browser-E2E boundaries. The implementation branch is `refactor/configured-test-harness`, targeting `feat/jiuwenswarm`. It has been rebased onto target revision `9670568` and includes the latest three browser files and all 27 contract scenarios.

- Configuration inventory: 92 execution entries and 48 suites; static inventory currently contains 437 assets.
- PR policy: 7 required execution entries. Daily policy: 82 required entries and 54 observational contract entries (27 × two executor labels).
- Browser collection compared against the latest target: 90 upstream framework-expanded tests versus 88 retained tests in 47 files. The only removals are the two explicitly approved obsolete declarations. Both the original snapshot and upstream integration are recorded in `test/support/migration.json`.
- Validation before PR submission: 65 harness/contract-tooling tests, 53 CI self-tests and 19 architecture tests passed; architecture boundaries and documentation lint/link checks also passed. These checks and framework collection are not a full product E2E run. Remote workflow execution must be assessed separately; existing product failures are not waived by this refactor.
- New configuration, scheduling and usage documentation is in `test/README.md` in the implementation branch.

## Configured subject models and assertions

Every case now explicitly declares `assertions.mode`: `deterministic`, `llm`, or `hybrid`. Real subject models are configured independently from judge models:

```yaml
llm:
  mode: real
  model:
    protocol: chat-completions
    baseUrlEnv: E2E_LLM_BASE_URL
    modelEnv: E2E_LLM_MODEL
    apiKeyEnv: E2E_LLM_TOKEN
assertions:
  mode: hybrid
  judge:
    model:
      protocol: chat-completions
      baseUrlEnv: E2E_JUDGE_BASE_URL
      modelEnv: E2E_JUDGE_MODEL
      apiKeyEnv: E2E_JUDGE_TOKEN
    timeoutSeconds: 60
    maxTokens: 1200
    maxInputCharacters: 24000
    rubric:
      - id: task-completion
        description: The answer and supplied artifact meet the requested task.
        threshold: 0.8
```

A model profile accepts exactly one literal `model` or `modelEnv`; each case may bind different environment names. Credentials are never stored in YAML. The initial transport is OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions; scoring requires a model supporting its temperature/max-token parameters.

Browser cases use `assessment.check(name, callback)` for configurable programmatic assertions and `assessment.submit({task, answer, artifacts, context})` for actual bounded evidence. Deterministic mode runs checks without a judge call. LLM-only mode skips those optional assertion callbacks. Hybrid mode requires at least one successful named check and all judge thresholds to pass. Ordinary framework `expect` calls remain mandatory structural/workflow guards. Never put setup/actions inside the optional assertion callback.

Judging runs only after the test body passes. Missing evidence, missing model configuration, malformed/missing/duplicate scores, low scores, HTTP errors and timeouts cannot produce PASS. There is no automatic fallback or retry. Every criterion has an explicit threshold in [0,1]. The configured input limit rejects oversized evidence rather than silently truncating it. Reports include per-attempt assessment attachments, resolved subject/judge identities, sanitized evidence, rubric, scores, reasons, usage when supplied and latency. A framework pass without required scoring evidence is rejected by the harness. Qualitative scoring does not prove numerical correctness; keep objective calculations checked programmatically.

The initial production example is `e2e.browser.model-request`: real subject + hybrid completion/delivery checks and report-quality scoring. The other two existing real-browser files retain deterministic assertions. All non-browser runners currently support deterministic assertions; unsupported scoring/runner combinations fail configuration validation explicitly.

## Daily real-model execution and setup

`test-daily.yml` invokes independent `external:none` and `external:real` jobs through the same reusable workflow. The external tag is derived from **either** a real subject or a live judge, so stub-subject/live-judge cases cannot accidentally enter the deterministic job. PR remains deterministic and receives no model secrets.

All three real-browser files run daily on both native and JiuwenSwarm as required work: six added entries. Daily now expands to **136 entries: 82 required and 54 observational contracts**. PR remains seven required entries. The real job explicitly sets `CI_ALLOW_REAL=1`; missing credentials cause required work to fail with unmet prerequisites.

Configure these repository Actions secrets for the supplied profiles:

- `E2E_LLM_BASE_URL`, `E2E_LLM_MODEL`, `E2E_LLM_TOKEN`.
- `E2E_JUDGE_BASE_URL`, `E2E_JUDGE_MODEL`, `E2E_JUDGE_TOKEN`.

Custom case-specific environment names must also be wired into the workflow. The implementation does not create secrets or choose a paid provider. Inspect with `pnpm test:list --profile daily --tag external:real --json`; with the six values exported and the isolated stack prerequisites ready, use `CI_ALLOW_REAL=1 pnpm test:daily --tag external:real`.

`literature-review` now registers/selects the configured model rather than hardcoded DeepSeek profiles; it still depends on its Skill/connector fixtures and PubMed availability. Those remaining requirements can block daily runs. Real-project Playwright traces are disabled because registration request bodies contain model keys; step screenshots and sanitized scoring evidence remain.

Local validation includes actual Playwright fixture execution against a local HTTP judge: three expected passes, three deliberate failures (native check, missing evidence, low score), three scoring requests and five assessment attachments. This verifies execution/reporting integration without calling an external model. No real-provider or complete product E2E pass is claimed: subject/judge variables were absent in the local environment during validation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every maintained test asset maps to an execution entry point or an explicit, reviewable exclusion/gate.
- [ ] The Python adapter suite, all seven standalone API/Runner journeys, and all eleven existing contract scenarios are represented; their tooling self-tests are classified separately.
- [ ] A nested Web `.test.ts`/`.test.tsx` file and a deeper Node module test are discovered without editing package-specific glob depths.
- [ ] Browser discovery does not execute Node tooling tests or collect helpers as journeys.
- [ ] Local and CI commands resolve to the same selected test set for the same profile and capabilities.
- [ ] Unknown IDs, unintended zero-test selections, stale entries, and unsupported executor requests cannot produce a misleading green result.
- [ ] Missing credentials/hardware are reported explicitly; no live-model invocation is enabled implicitly by listing or selecting a full profile.
- [ ] Reports distinguish selected, executed, failed, blocked, skipped, and unexecuted cases and identify the actual executor.
- [ ] Before/after discovery mappings account for the existing browser cases, standalone journeys, and contract scenarios. Reclassification is recorded explicitly; tests are not lost to preserve a green count.
- [ ] Existing public commands have documented compatibility or migration behavior, with a single repository testing guide explaining where tests belong and how to run them.
- [ ] Focused regression checks cover discovery, selection, compatibility wrappers, empty/missing cases, and truthful failure propagation.

## Follow-up work

A complete service-lifecycle/isolation harness, product compatibility fixes, broad legacy remediation, new ST/E2E coverage, coverage-percentage thresholds, automated nightly failure triage should be handled separately; real-model judging is now included in the agreed implementation scope above. This issue establishes the shared entry points and discovery guarantees those improvements depend on.

### 📚 Documentation Issue Description

> Related: #116 (first-run installation troubleshooting), #118 (capability entries), #119 (entry-point order). The landing pages and the bucket definitions overlap with #119's navigation ask, so this issue owns their delivery and #119 owns the ordering.

## Summary

PR 122 reorganizes the docs into six buckets per language, but the scaffolding that makes a bucket usable is missing. Five of the six buckets have no landing page, the meaning of each bucket is written only in the PR description, and the user tree has no security page, no general FAQ and no glossary. I would like these standard pages added on top of the structure PR 122 ships.

## Current state

Verified against PR #122 head f1e18c5:

- Twelve content directories (six buckets, two languages), and only `developer-docs` has a README in each language. `getting-started`, `core`, `domains`, `how-to` and `reference` have none, so a reader who jumps to a bucket lands on a bare file list.
- What each bucket is for exists only in the PR 122 description. `docs/README.md` names the six buckets in one sentence and defines none of them. Names like `core` and `domains` are not self-explanatory.
- No security or trust page exists in the user tree. The only security text is the multi-user WARNING in `README.md:7-8`, which covers loopback binding, the single bearer token, the absence of TLS and the sandbox boundary. The one page that explains isolation, `sandbox-execution.md`, sits in `docs/en/developer-docs/` and `docs/zh/developer-docs/`.
- No general troubleshooting or FAQ page exists. The only troubleshooting content is the Docker section inside `docs/en/getting-started/deployment.md`. The first-run, installation-recovery path is already asked for in #116, which is narrower than a general FAQ.
- No glossary exists. Terms such as Project and Session (used in `docs/en/getting-started/quick-start.md:48`), and Skill, Specialist, Connector, Reviewer and workspace (used across `docs/en/reference/runtime-behavior.md`), have no single definition a new reader can look up.

## What to write

1. Section landing pages. Add a `README.md` to each of the five index-less buckets in both languages, using one template: what this bucket is for, when a reader should come here, and one line for each child page.
2. Bucket definitions. Write the six definitions into `docs/README.md`, so the classification rule lives in the repository and not only in the pull request.
3. Security and trust page. Add a user-facing page in both languages that states the loopback and single-token defaults, the absence of TLS, the fail-closed sandbox and what runs outside it, and the "not a multi-user service" boundary. Link `docs/en/developer-docs/sandbox-execution.md` for depth instead of repeating it.
4. General troubleshooting and FAQ. Add a page in both languages covering model connection failures, permission cards, connector and proxy failures, run timeouts, and where data lives. Keep first-run installation recovery in #116 and link to it.
5. Glossary. Add a page in both languages defining at least Project, Session, Skill, Specialist, Connector, Reviewer and workspace, and link it from the language index.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each of `getting-started`, `core`, `domains`, `how-to` and `reference` has a landing page in both languages, following one template.
- [ ] `docs/README.md` defines what each of the six buckets is for.
- [ ] A security and trust page exists in both user trees and links the sandbox design page.
- [ ] A general troubleshooting or FAQ page exists in both languages and is distinct from the first-run recovery in #116.
- [ ] A glossary page defines at least Project, Session, Skill, Specialist, Connector, Reviewer and workspace.
- [ ] Each new page is linked from its language index, and each landing page links its child pages.

## Open questions

- Should the bucket definitions live in `docs/README.md`, in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, or on a dedicated documentation-style page?
- Does the security page need maintainer sign-off on what is safe to claim before it is published?
- Should the glossary be one page per language, or a section of the documentation home?

## Out of scope

- Page frontmatter and a page status or version schema.
- A machine-readable `llms.txt` or `llms-full.txt` export.
- Changelog or release-notes pages.
- Contributor guides for adding a tool, skill, connector or provider.
- These lower-priority page types are recorded in the audit's deferred list and are not tracked here.

### Improvement and Fix Suggestions

_No response_

### 📚 Documentation Issue Description

> Related: #55 (owns the evolve pages in both languages), #118 (owns the English Idea Tree page and records product status).

## Summary

The Chinese tree has ten pages with no English counterpart, the English tree now has three pages with no Chinese counterpart, and readers cannot tell whether a missing language means "not translated yet", "internal", or "unsupported". I would like each gap classified and then closed, translated, or labeled.

## Current state

Verified against PR #122 head f1e18c5:

- `docs/en/` has 38 pages and `docs/zh/` has 45.
- Ten Chinese-only pages. Nine sit under `docs/zh/developer-docs/` and one under `docs/zh/core/`:

  ```text
  docs/zh/developer-docs/evolve-standalone.md
  docs/zh/developer-docs/plugins.md
  docs/zh/developer-docs/runner-inheritance.md
  docs/zh/developer-docs/session-trajectory.md
  docs/zh/developer-docs/skill-library-management.md
  docs/zh/developer-docs/skill-library-management-mvp.md
  docs/zh/developer-docs/skill-library-management-m1.md
  docs/zh/developer-docs/skill-library-management-m2.md
  docs/zh/developer-docs/skill-self-evolution.md
  docs/zh/core/idea-tree.md
  ```

- Three English-only pages, all under `docs/en/developer-docs/`: `context-assembly.md`, `context-assembly-examples.md` and `runtime-core.md`. The path move introduced this gap: they were language-neutral under `docs/architecture/`, so before the reorg both language trees could reach them and now the Chinese tree cannot. `docs/en/developer-docs/agent-backend.md:273` and `docs/zh/developer-docs/agent-backend.md:273` also still say `docs/architecture/context-assembly.md`, a path that no longer exists. Those are plain-text references, so the link check added by PR 122 does not catch them. Fixing this is content work for a later step, recorded here because it is a real gap in the shipped tree.
- The PR 122 body itself lists bilingual semantic drift as follow-up work, so this issue does not own the content alignment of shared pages.

## What to write

1. Classify the nine pages under `docs/zh/developer-docs/`. Two are owned elsewhere: `evolve-standalone.md` stays with #55, and the skill-library drafts are recorded here while their consolidation stays with the PR follow-up. The pages that need a disposition here are `plugins.md`, `runner-inheritance.md`, `session-trajectory.md`, `skill-self-evolution.md` and the four skill-library-management files. Each is either translated (public), labeled as an internal design note, or retired. The public status comes from the capability-entries issue (#118).
2. Classify `docs/zh/core/idea-tree.md`. The English counterpart or replacement is owned by #118, so this issue records only the page-level disposition and the status label.
3. Give the three English-only pages their own decision: restore them to a language-neutral location, add Chinese counterparts, or label them English-only. In every case, fix the two dead references at `docs/en/developer-docs/agent-backend.md:273` and `docs/zh/developer-docs/agent-backend.md:273` to point at the new location.
4. Add a status label to every page that has no counterpart in one language, so a reader can tell "not translated" from "internal".
5. Add the missing language counterpart for every page classified as public.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each of the eight pages owned by this issue has a recorded disposition (translated, labeled internal, or retired), with maintainer sign-off for the unconfirmed ones.
- [ ] `docs/zh/core/idea-tree.md` has a recorded disposition, and the English page or replacement is delivered by #118.
- [ ] The three English-only pages have a recorded decision, and `docs/en/developer-docs/agent-backend.md:273` and `docs/zh/developer-docs/agent-backend.md:273` no longer cite `docs/architecture/`.
- [ ] English counterparts exist for the pages classified as public, and Chinese counterparts exist where the decision is to translate.
- [ ] Every page without a counterpart in one language carries a status label.
- [ ] Pages delivered by #117 and #118 land in both languages.

## Open questions

- Public status of plugins, runner inheritance, session trajectory, skill-self-evolution and the skill-library design notes (same confirmation as #118).
- Can the superseded `skill-library-management-m1` / `m2` / `mvp` drafts be retired, or should they be kept as history?
- Should the three former `docs/architecture/` pages return to a language-neutral directory, or is an English-only page with a clear label acceptable?

## Out of scope

- Semantic drift between shared pages such as `mcp-tool-protocol.md`, `subagent-orchestration.md` and `deployment.md`. PR 122 lists that as a content-owner follow-up, so it is not an acceptance criterion here.
- How a page without a counterpart is displayed on any downstream site. The public site repository is deferred for now.
- Translating internal design notes before their public status is confirmed.
- The English Idea Tree page (owned by #118) and the evolve sidecar disposition (owned by #55).
