# [Docs]: Deliver the first tutorial batch: analyze a dataset, run a literature search

> First batch of the tutorial series proposed in #26. Related: #22.

## Summary

#26 proposes a tutorial series and runnable quick-start cases. PR #122 removed the
tutorial directory in both languages, so the first batch needs a new landing place and a
new numbering rule. I propose extending `getting-started/` as the learning path and
dropping numeric file prefixes, then making the quick start's first task concrete, adding
a short model-setup page, and adding two tutorials that end in a verifiable result. The
later #26 batches (skills, MCP connector, and result-tracing tutorials) stay in #26.

## Current state

- Neither language has a tutorial directory at PR #122 head f1e18c5. The learning-style
  evolve walkthrough is now `docs/en/domains/evolve-a-solution.md` (119 lines) and
  `docs/zh/domains/evolve-a-solution.md` (85 lines). The only long end-to-end case is
  `docs/en/domains/literature-research.md` (212 lines, ZH 210).
- Quick start is `docs/en/getting-started/quick-start.md` (62 lines) and
  `docs/zh/getting-started/quick-start.md` (64 lines). Section 4, "Run a first scientific
  task" (lines 46-54), now has five steps that name a CSV or PDF, the permission card, the
  message timeline, and the Artifact area. It still gives no single named input, no exact
  prompt worth copying, and no description of what a correct result looks like.
- Model setup is quick start section 3 (lines 42-44). There is no page that walks through
  the settings UI (model registry, global defaults, connection test) or the failure path.
- Quick start's Next steps (lines 56-62) links deployment, configuration, runtime
  behavior, built-in tools, and `developer-docs/architecture.md`. It links no first-task
  tutorial. The language indexes list getting-started with two entries
  (`docs/en/README.md` lines 9-10, `docs/zh/README.md` lines 9-10).

## What to write

First batch, in both languages.

1. Rework quick start section 4 into one concrete task: a named small input, the exact
   prompt, and the expected visible result.
2. Landing proposal. Put the new tutorials in `getting-started/` and drop the numeric
   prefixes. PR #122 assigns `getting-started` the job of install, deployment, and first
   successful task, and it added no empty buckets, so extend it rather than revive
   `tutorial/`. Proposed files:
   - `docs/en/getting-started/analyze-a-dataset.md` and
     `docs/zh/getting-started/analyze-a-dataset.md` (new)
   - `docs/en/getting-started/literature-search-and-report.md` and
     `docs/zh/getting-started/literature-search-and-report.md` (new)
   - `docs/en/getting-started/model-setup.md` and
     `docs/zh/getting-started/model-setup.md` (new)
   The existing evolve walkthrough stays at `domains/evolve-a-solution.md` and becomes the
   advanced follow-on. If maintainers prefer a separate `tutorials/` bucket, keep the same
   descriptive slugs there. I am stating this as a proposal, not a decision.
3. Each tutorial states its prerequisites (a working model configuration), its expected
   result, and links deeper reference pages instead of copying them.
4. The model-setup page walks through model registry, global defaults, the connection
   test, and what to do when the connection fails.
5. Update `docs/en/README.md` and `docs/zh/README.md` to list the new tutorials, and point
   quick start's Next steps at `docs/en/domains/evolve-a-solution.md` plus the two new
   tutorials.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Quick start section 4 names a concrete input, an exact prompt, and the expected
  visible result (EN + ZH).
- [ ] `getting-started/analyze-a-dataset.md` and
  `getting-started/literature-search-and-report.md` exist in both languages, each
  completable with a working model configuration and ending with something the reader can
  point at.
- [ ] `getting-started/model-setup.md` takes a reader from a fresh install to a tested
  model connection, or quick start section 3 is expanded to do the same.
- [ ] Each tutorial shows its first permission card and where the output lands.
- [ ] The tutorials link the literature case and the reference pages instead of copying

> Complements the still-open #46 (its release-link, verification, ordering, and naming
> asks are tracked there). Related: #1, #27, #29, #35, #38.

## Summary

The documentation now sends a new Linux reader to a single deployment guide, but nothing
helps that reader choose among the three modes, prepare the right host, or recover when
the first run fails. The README installation section is one paragraph that delegates to
the guide. I would like that decision path written down, in both languages.

## Current state

- `README.md` (57 lines) and `README_zh.md` route installation to
  `docs/en/getting-started/deployment.md` and `docs/zh/getting-started/deployment.md`.
  The installation section (README lines 38-40) names neither a release asset nor a mode,
  and the Requirements table (lines 30-34) is the only place that ties modes to operating
  systems.
- The guide is 427 lines in English and 451 in Chinese at PR #122 head f1e18c5. It opens
  with a three-mode comparison (EN lines 5-15). The table columns are Mode, What the user
  receives, Host dependencies, and Intended use (line 7). No column states supported
  operating systems.
- Operating-system support is scattered. The binary artifact names appear at lines 24-25,
  local mode says it supports Linux x86_64/aarch64 and macOS x64/arm64 at line 131, and
  the Docker prerequisites say Linux x86_64 or aarch64 at line 173.
- The binary section opens with "Build and run" (line 19) and teaches building the
  artifact from source. Nothing in the guide walks a reader from a published release asset
  to `serve`.
- The local service token versus a model API key is explained in the README (line 51) and
  the quick start (`docs/en/getting-started/quick-start.md`, line 30). Token rejection
  recovery appears in the quick start and in the Docker FAQ (deployment guide line 390),
  but the README links neither passage. #35 shows the confusion is real.
- The guide's only FAQ-style troubleshooting sits inside the Docker section (lines
  378-408: build failures, data-directory permissions, port conflicts, token rejection,
  degraded health, sandbox failures). Binary mode documents Bubblewrap (lines 64-77) and
  local mode carries a Seatbelt note (lines 134 and 161), but neither mode has an FAQ
  covering token rejection, degraded health, or port conflicts. The quick start explains a
  `degraded` status at line 38 without linking a recovery passage.
- #1 asked how to obtain the binary. #46 asked for release links, SHA-256 verification
  instructions, a deployment guide led by downloading rather than building, and aligned
  configuration entry names. The decision and recovery layers above are still open.

## What to write

1. A short "choose your installation path" block in the README installation section,
   before it delegates to the guide: one line each for the prepackaged binary, source
   mode, and Docker, saying who each is for, with links into the matching deployment-guide
   section. Mirrored in `README_zh.md`.
2. Add an explicit operating-system column to the mode comparison in both guides (binary:
   Linux x86_64/aarch64, source: Linux and macOS, Docker: Linux), and lead the guide's
   binary section with downloading a published asset before the build-from-source
   procedure. This is the remaining ordering ask of #46.
3. A first-run troubleshooting block for binary and local modes (Docker already has one),
   covering at least: token rejected and where the Connection settings live, a `degraded`
   health status and what it means for the Runner, a missing `bwrap`, and where the logs
   are. Linked from the README.
4. Wherever a download command appears, link the Releases page rather than a pinned
   version URL, so the text survives the next release.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] README (EN + ZH) states who should pick binary, source, or Docker before it sends
  readers to the guide.
- [ ] The mode comparison in both deployment guides states the supported operating systems
  per mode.
- [ ] The binary and local modes have a first-run troubleshooting block in both languages,
  linked from the README or quick start.
- [ ] Any download command links the Releases page rather than a pinned version URL.
- [ ] The English and Chinese paths describe the same confirmed behavior and platform
  matrix.

## Open questions

- Is Docker positioned as an equal path for new users, or as an advanced option? This
  decides how prominent it is in the decision block.
- The packaging output includes `SHA256SUMS`. Confirm whether the published release assets
  carry it, and if so, add the verification step #46 asked for.
- Do update and uninstall instructions belong in the deployment guide now, or in a later
  pass?
- Should this issue absorb #46's remaining verification and ordering asks, or leave them
  with #46? Maintainers' call.

## Out of scope

- Changing the release process or adding build artifacts.
- Documenting unsupported platforms.
- The product fixes tracked in #29, #35, and #38. This issue only links their recovery
  documentation.
- Reordering the documentation indexes (tracked separately).

## Background

ScienceDiscovery is strengthening its end-to-end test coverage. We want to collect the complete user journeys that the community believes must remain continuously protected.

This RFC does not prescribe an implementation. It focuses on four questions: **What task is the user trying to complete? What outcomes must be observable? Does the scenario require a real model? Should it run as a pull-request gate or as a scheduled test?**

## How to contribute

Copy the comment template below and add one row for each proposed test scenario. Maintainers will periodically consolidate actionable feedback into the main table.

Guidelines:

- **Test scenario**: describe a complete flow from the user's goal, rather than an internal function or an isolated component.
- **Observations**: list user-visible outcomes and critical states, such as the final answer, tool calls, permissions, artifacts, citations, and recovery after a refresh.
- **Test method**: use `Mock LLM`, `Real LLM`, or `Both`, and explain why a real model is necessary when applicable.
- **Estimated token usage**: use `0 (scripted)` for Mock LLM cases; for Real LLM cases, estimate total input and output tokens for one run.
- **Estimated duration**: give the target duration for one case, excluding first-time dependency installation.
- **Priority**: use `P0` for basic platform availability, `P1` for core scientific capabilities, and `P2` for enhancements or corner cases.
- **Notes**: record environment requirements, external services, credentials, cost, side effects, candidate benchmark sources, or stability risks.

## Initial candidates

The following entries are both examples of the requested format and an initial backlog. The community is welcome to refine their priority, observations, estimates, and execution method.

| Test scenario | Observations | Test method (Mock or Real LLM) | Related feature | Estimated token usage | Estimated duration | Priority | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Basic multi-turn conversation and refresh recovery | The run completes; the second turn uses conversation history; message order, terminal state, and refreshed content remain consistent | Mock LLM | Session, Agent Loop, History, SSE | 0 (scripted) | 2–3 min | P0 | No external network |
| Tool call, permission, and continued reasoning | Permission moves from pending to allowed; the tool executes once; its result returns to the model; the Agent continues and finishes | Mock LLM | Tool, Permission, Runner, Agent Loop | 0 (scripted) | 2–3 min | P0 | Use a safe local tool fixture |
| Plan creation, update, and completion | Plan and step states remain ordered and correct; updates do not block tools; the final state persists and recovers | Mock LLM | Plan, Context, Workspace UI | 0 (scripted) | 2–3 min | P0 | Use a deterministic tool-call sequence |
| Subagent delegation and result return | The child Agent lifecycle is complete; tool ownership is correct; the result returns to the lead Agent; reasoning continues; refresh restores the state | Mock LLM | Subagent, Team, Tool, Context | 0 (scripted) | 3–4 min | P0 | No external provider |
| Generate and deliver an artifact | The file exists; deliverables are distinct from temporary files; preview and download work; provenance is traceable; the final answer references the artifact | Mock LLM | Workspace, Artifact, Provenance, Tool | 0 (scripted) | 3–4 min | P0 | Use a local Python or Shell environment |
| Literature review | The Agent searches multiple sources, retrieves and extracts selected papers, produces traceable citations, handles source failures, and delivers a review artifact | Both | MCP, Literature Sources, Governed Download, PDF Extraction, Citation, Review | 0 mocked; 20k–60k real | 10–30 min | P1 | Real run requires network access and may depend on source availability |
| Evolve a solution | The Agent defines an objective and evaluation, runs iterative candidates, preserves checkpoints and logs, compares results, and delivers the best reproducible solution | Both | Evolve, Runner, Artifact, Provenance, Review | 0 mocked; 15k–50k real | 10–30 min | P1 | Candidate source: Terminal-Bench-Science |
| Data analysis | The Agent inspects an input dataset, selects and executes a valid analysis, validates intermediate results, and delivers reproducible code, figures, and conclusions | Both | Workspace, Python/R, Artifact, Provenance, Review | 0 mocked; 10k–40k real | 10–25 min | P1 | Candidate source: BiomniBench-DA |
| AI model workflow | The Agent prepares valid model inputs, invokes the model workload, exposes execution progress, preserves outputs and environment metadata, and explains the result | Both | Scientific Environment, Runner, NPU, Artifact, Provenance | 0 mocked; 10k–40k real | 15–60 min | P1 | Candidate tools/models: Protenix, ProteinMPNN, and similar workloads; hardware availability may constrain scheduling |
| Simulation tool workflow | The Agent prepares a valid simulation, invokes the selected simulator, reports progress and failures, and delivers reproducible configuration, logs, and results | Both | Scientific Environment, Runner, Tool, Artifact, Provenance | 0 mocked; 10k–40k real | 15–60 min | P1 | Real cases may require licensed software, large dependencies, or specialized hardware |
| Memory graph | Research outputs are written to the graph with correct identities and relations; retrieval returns relevant prior context; graph-backed citations remain traceable after refresh | Both | Memory Graph, Context, Provenance, Citation | 0 mocked; 8k–25k real | 5–20 min | P1 | Mocked case can use the local backend; scheduled case may use Neo4j |
| Agent team collaboration | The lead Agent decomposes work across multiple specialists; child scopes remain isolated; progress is observable; results return to the lead and are synthesized without loss or duplication | Both | Agent Team, Subagent, Context, Permission, Trajectory | 0 mocked; 15k–50k real | 10–30 min | P1 | Include concurrent child execution and one recoverable child failure |
| Idea Tree research | The Agent starts an Idea Tree run, expands and evaluates candidates, supports pause and resume, persists the tree, and delivers the selected result with its reasoning trail | Both | Idea Tree, Evolve, Workspace UI, Artifact, Provenance | 0 mocked; 15k–50k real | 10–30 min | P1 | Validate both tree state and the user-visible explorer |

## Comment template

Copy this table into a comment. Add more rows when proposing multiple scenarios.

| Test scenario | Observations | Test method (Mock or Real LLM) | Related feature | Estimated token usage | Estimated duration | Priority | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Describe the complete user journey | List user-visible outcomes and critical states | Mock LLM / Real LLM / Both | List related capabilities | Estimate | Estimate | P0 / P1 / P2 | Add environment, cost, dependency, or stability notes |

## Suggested areas

- Agent Loop, tools, permissions, planning, and Agent teams;
- MCP, skills, Web Search, and Web Fetch;
- literature retrieval, paper download, PDF extraction, and scientific databases;
- artifacts, provenance, evidence, claims, citations, and review;
- context compression, long-running task continuity, and error recovery;
- local and remote Runners, scientific environments, NPU workloads, and background tasks;
- settings, onboarding, observability, and critical usability journeys;
- scenarios that can reveal issues only with a Real LLM or a real external service.

## Expected outcome

Community feedback will form a prioritized E2E case backlog, divided into:

- fast Mocked E2E cases executed for every pull request;
- comprehensive Mocked and Real LLM E2E cases executed on a schedule;
- real scientific-task acceptance tests executed before a release.

This issue is for collecting and clarifying test requirements. Implementation can be split into follow-up issues and pull requests by scenario.

issue:84.body:
### 🚀 Background Description ScienceDiscovery's backend is currently the TypeScript `services/api` (port 4310, `http/index.ts` at about 3,500 lines, `store.ts` at about 5,600 lines, depending on about 50k lines of `packages/*`, with the agent loop also running in Node). The frontend `apps/web` talks to it through about 260 HTTP endpoints plus SSE. [JiuwenSwarm](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/jiuwenswarm) already provides general agent capabilities: multi-agent team/Swarm, skills and skill self-evolution, permission approval, sessions and projects, MCP, scheduled tasks, and the jiuwenbox sandbox. This issue proposes: **keep the existing TypeScript frontend, reuse JiuwenSwarm as the main Agent backend as much as possible, and keep the science-specific modules (evolve, idea-tree, memory-graph, artifact/provenance, etc.) as standalone backends.** E2E cases serve as the acceptance spec for the migration. ### Goals and plan **Short term (Sep 30):** 10 E2E cases pass with no quality regression, and the corresponding 10 scenarios are usable; release a minor-version RC. **October:** Refine step by step, complete the migration, and make all E2E cases usable. **Long term:** Gradually switch to the componentized version of JiuwenSwarm (the `AgentRuntime` public API) and evolve in sync with JiuwenSwarm; gate on contract tests, switching the chat core first and the remaining domains afterward. The 10 E2E cases will be decided by Zhang Yi by Sep 21. **Baseline version:** Fixed on JiuwenSwarm 0.2.6. The interface and event analysis in this issue was read from the local `0.2.5.beta1` code and needs to be rechecked against 0.2.6. ### Overall migration philosophy 1. **Reuse JiuwenSwarm first and do not modify it by default; intrusive modification is allowed when necessary.** Use its chat, sessions, team/Swarm, permissions, skills, MCP, and scheduled tasks directly. Intrusive modifications are applied as patches on the fixed version (0.2.6) and merged back upstream later. 2. **Keep the frontend contract unchanged and translate in one place only.** The frontend speaks HTTP + SSE (32 event types); JiuwenSwarm speaks WebSocket (`req / res / event`, about 400 methods). A new **adapter** does the translation, with essentially no frontend changes; the goal is to eliminate endpoints that need a wrapper to adapt. 3. **Scientific value stays in standalone backends.** artifact, provenance, review, evolve, idea-tree, memory-graph, and runner each have their own process, data directory, and token; the frontend reaches them through the adapter's reverse proxy, and the agent calls them through MCP tools. 4. **Each piece of state has exactly one owner.** Sessions and projects belong to JiuwenSwarm, science metadata belongs to each standalone service, and the adapter only handles what nobody else owns (run event log, settings and secrets, permission audit, usage statistics). 5. **Tests are the spec, and the agent implements by "red-to-green".** First turn the existing E2E and contract tests into an acceptance baseline that can target any backend, then implement feature domains one by one; behavior without a covering case does not count as migrated. 6. **Switching can be done in batches.** For routes not yet migrated, the adapter can fall back to the old `services/api` and switch traffic domain by domain (this requires both sides to share session IDs, see Open decisions). ### Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR UI["Web UI (apps/web, TypeScript, essentially unchanged)"] subgraph ADP["Adapter (newly written, Python)"] direction TB A1["HTTP + SSE routes (about 260)"] A2["Bearer auth, users mapped to user_id"] A3["run registry and event log (seq, resume)"] A4["Event mapping (32 frontend event types)"] A5["Storage for settings, secrets, permission audit, usage statistics"] end subgraph JW["JiuwenSwarm (reused, not forked)"] direction TB GW["Gateway /ws"] AS["AgentServer"] CAP["Sessions and projects / Team and Swarm / Permission rails
Skill and evolution / MCP client / Cron / jiuwenbox"] GW --> AS --> CAP end subgraph SVC["Standalone backends (own process, data directory, token)"] direction TB S1["artifact / provenance / CAS
extracted from services/api"] S2["evolve
Python already exists, TS orchestration layer moved in"] S3["idea-tree
split out of evolve"] S4["memory-graph
already a standalone service"] S5["paper parsing"] S6["runner + compute
environments, execution, remote hosts, NPU"] S7["science MCP services
biomedicine / UniProt / llm-wiki"] end UI -->|"HTTP + SSE"| ADP ADP -->|"WebSocket req / res / event"| GW ADP -->|"reverse proxy"| SVC CAP -->|"MCP tools"| SVC ADP -.->|"Fallback for unmigrated routes (optional)"| LEGACY["old services/api"] ``` In the short term the adapter connects to the Gateway's WebSocket (broadest coverage); in the long term it switches to the `AgentRuntime` componentized interface.
The two ways to connect the adapter, and a few facts about JiuwenSwarm's connection layer **The two ways to connect the adapter:** | | A. Connect to the Gateway's WebSocket (recommended for the first version) | B. Embed `AgentRuntime` in-process | |---|---|---| | Coverage | All about 400 methods, including team/swarm, skills, mcp, config | Only covers single-agent sessions, chat, permissions, and model and mode catalogs; the Process CLI docs explicitly do not accept Team / Workflow / AutoHarness root modes | | Types | Handwritten, no schema | Python dataclasses, typed | | Stability | Protocol is ready-made, validated by the React frontend and the TUI | Public API was only just completed (`f29c060c`, `8773691e`), stability unknown | **A few facts about JiuwenSwarm's connection layer (which the adapter must fill in itself):** - Identity comes from connection parameters (`user_id`, `session_id`, `mode`, `agent_id`, `app_id`) or request headers, and no token validation was found, so the frontend's existing Bearer auth must be done by the adapter. - `seq` and `stream_id` on event frames are optional fields, and no mechanism was found for replaying by sequence number after a disconnect, so the frontend's `runs/:id/events?after=N` resume relies on the adapter storing its own event log. - The payloads of `chat.delta / final / reasoning` are flat `{session_id, content}`; `chat.tool_call / tool_update / tool_result / ask_user_question / subtask_update / subagent_activity / usage_*` and similar keep their full payloads.
### Migration approach per module | Scope | Migration approach | |---|---| | Chat, sessions, projects, permissions, models, MCP, skills | **Reuse JiuwenSwarm + adapter mapping** (59 approximate mappings, 21 direct mappings) | | Runs and event log, settings and secrets, permission audit, skill library versions, usage statistics | **Adapter-built** (JiuwenSwarm has none, 66 items) | | Science toolset (run_shell, execute Python, web, artifact, etc.) | **Provided again as MCP** to JiuwenSwarm's agent (a new major item) | | artifact / provenance / CAS, review | **Standalone service**: reuse the existing TS packages plus a thin HTTP layer, no rewrite | | evolve, idea-tree, memory-graph, paper | **Standalone service**: the evolve orchestration layer moves into Python, idea-tree is split out of evolve, memory-graph is almost as is, paper gets a wrapper layer | | runner, environments, remote hosts, NPU | **Keep runner + pass through**; remote host and NPU logic moves out with runner, in the second batch | | Scheduled tasks, science gateway MCP | **Reuse directly** JiuwenSwarm's `schedule.*` and MCP config | | Frontend | Essentially unchanged; hide unsupported entry points and clean up dead code |
Full module migration table (current state → target → approach) Legend: **Reuse** = use JiuwenSwarm directly; **Adapt** = the adapter does the mapping; **Build ourselves** = JiuwenSwarm does not have it; **Standalone** = standalone backend; **Keep as is** = essentially untouched. | Module | Current state | Target | Migration approach | |---|---|---|---| | Chat and agent loop | `native-agent`: 128-round loop, parallel tools, loop-guard, deferred `tool_search` | JiuwenSwarm's agent loop | **Reuse + adapt**: `chat.send / interrupt / user_answer`; agent-core 的 `openjiuwen.harness` 导出公开工厂 **`create_deep_agent(...)`**（约 30 个关键字参数）与 `DeepAgentConfig`（50+ 字段，全部带文档）。JiuwenSwarm 的 `agent_adapter` 36,050 行里，`interface_code.py`（2,809，code `on_get_context_window`）、6 个内置压缩器 + 4 个卸载器。四个改造层级，均**零源码改动**： | 层级 | API | 能改什么 | |---|---|---| | L1 注入 | `AgentRail.before_model_call(ctx)` 改 `ModelCallInputs` | 加删消息、加 prompt section | | L2 换处理器 | `@ContextEngine.register_processor` | 压缩 / 召回 / 卸载算法本身 | | L3 换最终窗口 | `agent.context_engine.register_window_mutator(fn)`，`fn: (ModelContext, ContextWindow) -> Awaitable[ContextWindow]` | **最终送进推理的窗口** | | L4 换整个模型 | 实现 `ModelContext(ABC)` 子类 | 整个上下文语义 | L3 正好承接我们现有 `packages/context` 的「model-aware 原子窗口选择 + 最终校验」。**待验证**：`register_window_mutator` 的执行点是否确实在所有 processor 之后。 ### 5.2 多 agent 探索 `openjiuwen/agent_teams/workflow/engine/seam.py` 文件头原文： > "The provider seam: the indirection that lets the engine be swapped. … The engine installs its `EngineProvider` for the duration of a run; **a different implementation … can install its own provider instead, and workflow scripts never change**." API：`Provider(Protocol)` 覆盖 `agent()` / `parallel()` / `pipeline()` / `map_parallel()` / `agent_session()` / `human()` / `budget`，配 `use_provider(p) -> Token` / `reset_provider()`。因为存在 `contextvar` 里，**科学探索 run 与普通 run 可在同进程并存**。 于是把 `services/evolve` 的 PUCT 搜索或 `packages/idea-tree` 的想法树升级成多 agent 分支探索，做法是实现一个 `ScienceExploreProvider` 装上去，**workflow 脚本一行不改**。 另有按名覆盖：`register_subagent_provider(name, factory)` 的文档写明「a later registration for the same name overrides it」，内置探索子智能体名为 `core.explore_agent`。 ⚠️ 注意两张表语义相反：`harness/manifest/catalog.py` 的 `add_descriptor()`（元数据）**拒绝重名并抛 `ValueError`**；provider 注册表（工厂）**后注册覆盖**。要覆盖内置算法走 provider 注册表，不要重复同名的 `@harness_element` 声明。 --- ## 六、侵入分析 侵入要分三种： - **A 型（源码侵入）**：必须改 JiuwenSwarm 的文件 - **B 型（协商性侵入）**：不改今天的行为，但要求冻结或新增扩展点 - **C 型（反向侵入）**：不改 JiuwenSwarm 一行，但**它的运行期假设侵入我们**——改进程状态、强制数据目录布局、注入依赖树 前两种此前讨论过，**C 型是这轮新发现的，也是「按块复用」的真正门槛**。 ### 6.1 C 型：三个全局副作用源 **(1) `jiuwenswarm/common/config.py` 在导入期修改 `sys.path`**（第 48–57 行）： ```python _user_config = os.getenv("JIUWENSWARM_CONFIG_DIR") if _user_config: _CONFIG_MODULE_DIR = Path(_user_config) elif get_config_dir().exists(): _CONFIG_MODULE_DIR = get_config_dir() if str(_CONFIG_MODULE_DIR) not in sys.path: sys.path.insert(0, str(_CONFIG_MODULE_DIR)) # 插到最前 ``` 进程级、导入即生效、不可撤销。若该目录含同名 `.py` 会**静默 shadow** 我们的模块；且行为取决于环境变量与目录是否存在，同一份代码在不同机器上 `config/config.yaml`、`agent/workspace/` 等结构。我们若 import 依赖它的块，就必须在自己的数据目录下再造一个最小 JiuwenSwarm 工作区。 **(3) 依赖树注入**：`workswarm` 的 `dependencies` 含 `create_deep_agent()` 跑通一次带工具调用 + 审批中断 + 流式的会话，并映射成现有 37 类 SSE | 自建装配的 4,000–8,000 行估算是否成立 | | ② | `register_window_mutator` 注入的受保护段，能否存活到最终 LLM 窗口（构造一个会被内置压缩器改写的长会话） | 上下文三语义能否等价迁移，还是要接受行为回退 | | ③ | 实现一个最小 `Provider` 并 `use_provider()`，验证 workflow 原语被整体替换后行为正确 | 科学探索能否成为多 agent 范式 | | ④ | `pip install workswarm` 后做依赖裁剪试验，量出可接受的最小依赖集 | M2 各块的分发成本 | 判据 ①③④ 直接决定路线，判据 ② 决定产品行为是否回退。**在第 0 阶段之前讨论总工期意义不大。** --- ## 九、待决定事项 1. **复用边界**：agent-core 直接依赖（本 issue）还是经 JiuwenSwarm Gateway（#84）。建议在 M0-a 一并验证后再定。 2. **是否采用 jiuwenbox**：采用则获得 Landlock、cgroup、推理隐私代理，但 **macOS 源码模式会失去沙箱**（jiuwenbox Linux-only）。需要产品明确。 3. **是否接 Skill 包管理**：涉及 6.2 的高 C 型侵入，三个选择需要拍板。 4. **控制面语言**：本方案保持 `services/api` 为 Node（保全约 81% 后端代码）。若未来要合并为单一 Python 后端，M0–M2 完成后可平滑过渡，但会额外触发 A3。 5. **差异化定位**：如果本项目的差异化主要在科学域能力（工具、连接器、证据溯源、科学环境、NPU），现有分层足够；如果在 agent 算法本身（上下文、探索、检索、演进），则应进一步收紧对 agent-core 的直接控制。这决定第 5 节各层级的使用频度。 --- ### 补充说明 - 本 issue 的全部结论来自上述基线 commit 的只读代码盘点，**未改动任何仓库**，未建分支、未提 PR。 - 归属用的「依赖率」是「模块内 import `openjiuwen` 的 `.py` 文件数 / 该模块 `.py` 文件总数」，是**代理指标**而非逻辑占比的精确度量；每条归属结论另有行数对照或具体文件路径佐证。 - C 型侵入的判定口径是「模块文件是否 import `jiuwenswarm.common.config` / `jiuwenswarm.common.utils`」，是传递依赖的一级近似；真正接入前应在 M0/M2 用一次真实 import 验证完整传递闭包。 - 与 #84 互为补充，不替代。

> Cross-tracking: [GitCode #26](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/26) (Chinese original of this issue). ### 🚀 Background Description Research agents often produce scripts, logs, configs, and prose (`.py`, `.r`, `.sh`, `.txt`, `.log`, `.yaml`, `.toml`, `.sql`, …). Users need to read those files in the artifact panel, not download them or jump to a new browser tab. The current viewer has two gaps: 1. **Plain-text artifacts have almost no in-app preview.** Catalog kinds only cover dataset / figure / html / json / latex / markdown / notebook / report / structure. Files such as `.py`, `.txt`, and `.log` fall into `other`. `ArtifactModal` loads only a few scientific kinds as text; `other` has no preview branch, so opening them is often a blank panel. In the workspace file sidebar, only `.md` uses the in-app Markdown reader; everything else is handed to `window.open` and the browser. 2. **Existing source / raw views are not a code-reading experience.** JSON, LaTeX source, Markdown source, CSV raw, and notebook code are plain `
`: no language highlighting, no line numbers, and long files are hard to scan or compare.

The viewer should:

- open plain-text files in-app;
- syntax-highlight common file types;
- show line numbers.

This is a viewing-experience request only. It does not change artifact registration, versioning, or provenance semantics.

### Design Ideas

Keep the existing specialized previews (Markdown render, tables, images, PDF/HTML iframe, molecular structure, notebook cells). Add one shared path for “read as source.”

Suggested behavior:

- Open recognizable UTF-8 text in-app — not a blank panel, and not a new browser tab by default.
- Pick a highlight language from the extension (and `mediaType` if needed). At least cover common research/engineering types:
  - plain text: `.txt`, `.log`, `.out`, `.err`
  - code: `.py`, `.r` / `.R`, `.jl`, `.js`, `.ts`, `.jsx`, `.tsx`, `.sh` / `.bash`, `.sql`, `.c` / `.h` / `.cpp`, `.java`, `.go`, `.rs`
  - config / data source: `.json`, `.yaml` / `.yml`, `.toml`, `.ini`, `.xml`, `.css`, `.html`
  - document source: `.md`, `.tex`
- Unmatched extensions that are still text: show as plain text, still with line numbers.
- Binaries, images, PDFs, Office files, etc. keep the current specialized viewer or download; do not force them through a text decoder.
- Markdown / table / notebook specialized previews stay; their “Source / Raw” views should reuse the same highlight + line-number component.
- Oversized files keep truncated preview (reuse the existing ~100_000 character cap) and tell the user they can download the full file.
- Highlighter library and whether to add `kind=text/code` are implementation choices, as long as the user gets highlighted text with line numbers. Do not change the artifact catalog or provenance semantics just to enable highlighting.

Out of scope:

- editing or saving files in the viewer;
- turning every file into a source view (images still show as images, CSVs still show as tables);
- a full IDE (folding, go-to-definition, diagnostics).

### Involved Public APIs

No new public HTTP API is expected. The viewer should keep using the existing artifact-version content and workspace-file read endpoints.

Possible internal adjustments (for implementation, not a product contract):

- load `other` / uncategorized text as text instead of skipping it as binary;
- if extension classification gains a `text`/`code` kind, use it only for preview routing and do not change the meaning of existing scientific kinds.

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- Artifact panel `ArtifactModal`: main catalog preview; `other` text must be readable.
- Workspace file tree: clicking `.py` / `.txt` etc. should open the same in-app text view, not only a new browser tab.
- Existing source views: JSON raw, Markdown/LaTeX source, CSV raw, notebook code, provenance scripts/logs — good candidates to reuse the same component.
- Artifact classification (`classifyScientificArtifact`): there is no text/code kind today; do not mis-label `.py` as dataset/report.
- i18n: new buttons / empty states / truncation copy must go through the existing message catalog.
- E2E: artifact panel, workspace file open, and existing Markdown/table/structure previews all need regression.

### Test Design and Test Plan

Functional:

- Open `.txt`: in-app full text (or truncation notice), line numbers; highlighting optional.
- Open `.py` / `.yaml` / `.json` and other common types: matching syntax highlighting, line numbers aligned with source lines (at least line 1 and the last visible line).
- Unknown extension, UTF-8 text: still opens as plain text with line numbers.
- Images, PDFs, structure files, other non-text: unchanged, not treated as source.
- Markdown artifacts: default remains rendered; Source view has highlighting and line numbers.
- Huge text: preview truncates, offers download, page stays responsive.
- Empty file: stable empty state, no error.

Regression:

- Markdown reports, CSV/JSON tables, images, HTML, notebooks, and molecular-structure previews still work.
- Workspace `.md` still uses the Markdown reader.
- Artifact download, version switching, and the provenance page still work.

Web E2E (required after changing the user-visible viewer):

- Open a text artifact in the panel; screenshot the highlighted, numbered end state.
- Open `.py` or `.txt` from the workspace tree; confirm in-app viewing rather than relying only on a new browser tab.
- Regression on one existing specialized preview (Markdown or CSV).

Formal E2E must not use the human trial port 4310 or its fixed data directory.

### Additional Information

Original request: support viewing plain-text artifacts, syntax highlighting for common file types, and line numbers.
